quotes.excerpt: But the Pearl of Great Price tells us that God ordained that his spirit children should pass through three estates, and we here who are his spirit children, and others, have passed from a former estate. … If they are faithful they will rise to exaltation and glory in their third estate, as already mentioned.
quotes.note: Untagged, for the same reason as clawson-three-estates-1937-q1: spirit → mortal → exaltation, with no tier behind the spirit and no account of how the spirit children came to be spirit children. Four years after clawson-glorified-man-1935 and two after clawson-three-estates-1937 the scheme is verbally identical, which is the finding — this is a fixed formula in the President of the Twelve's repertoire, not a developing position. “His spirit children” names the relation twice in one sentence and explains it neither time. The elision covers roughly eight paragraphs on the war in heaven, Lucifer's rebellion, and the second estate as a school of experience.

notes: Re-pulled verbatim from the Pulpit vault file talks/english/conference-reports/1939/1939-04-rudger-clawson-purpose-in-life-brings-happiness.md and re-verified against the archive.org djvu text of conferencereport1939a. Conference Report, so hearsay A; the title is supplied by the vault. Third and last of Clawson's purpose-of-life addresses in this batch and the only one that reaches the forward axis, which it does in the final two paragraphs before the closing verse — the doctrinal content is an appendix to a discourse whose main body is premortal rebellion and evil spirits seeking to steal bodies.

title: Joseph Fielding Smith: “the deaths” defined as being denied the privilege of eternal increase
speaker: Joseph Fielding Smith
office: Of the Council of the Twelve Apostles; Church Historian and Recorder
venue: General conference, first day afternoon session (Conference Report, April 1941)

quotes.excerpt: Now, again, the Lord continues, in this revelation, to say that if they are married by His word, then they shall pass on to the exaltation, and that exaltation is a fulness and a continuation of the seeds forever. In other words, the family organization is intact throughout all eternity, and there shall be eternal increase, — and that is the crowning glory, if you please, in the Kingdom of God.
quotes.note: The gloss on D&C 132:19, and the reason this is euphemism rather than explicit: Smith decodes “a continuation of the seeds forever” into two things — the family organization enduring, and “eternal increase” — and neither of them names offspring, spirit children, or any mechanism. A hearer who did not already know what increase consisted of would learn nothing here except that the family survives death.

quotes.excerpt: What do you get of that? This fact, that the marriage for eternity grants unto us the privilege of eternal lives. It does not have reference to our existence hereafter, for every man will live eternally; it is the continuation of the seeds forever, which constitutes eternal lives.
quotes.note: The distinction Smith is at pains to draw — “eternal lives” is not immortality, which everyone gets, but the continuation of the seeds. He rules out the weak reading of the phrase and then declines to state the strong one in any concrete terms.

quotes.excerpt: What is meant by the expression “to the deaths”? It means to be stopped, to be shut off, to be denied the privilege of eternal increase. That is the deaths, and a great majority of mankind will go on into the eternity, to partake of the deaths, which means a stoppage, cutting off from these great blessings, which shall be bestowed upon those who are willing to keep the commandments of the Lord.
quotes.note: The negative definition, and the one that gives the entry its weight: D&C 132:25's “the deaths” is glossed as the loss of eternal increase, which makes increase the very thing exaltation consists of. Compare eldred-smith-no-increase-1948 and jfs-agq-temple-marriage-1954 — the doctrine keeps arriving in this shape, as the penalty for marrying outside the temple rather than as a description of what the exalted do.

notes: Re-pulled verbatim from the Pulpit vault file talks/english/conference-reports/1941/1941-04-joseph-fielding-smith-keeping-the-commandments-important.md and checked word-for-word against the Church History Library preservation scan of the printed Conference Report on the Internet Archive (conferencereport1941a, djvu text, discourse beginning at leaf n36); the em dash in “eternal increase, — and that is the crowning glory” is the printed reading. Conference Report, so A; historical-official. The printed Report supplies no formal title; the vault's is taken from the printed side-heads. The whole address is an anti–civil-marriage sermon aimed at parents (“I would rather not receive it,” of wedding invitations outside the temple), and the eternal-increase doctrine appears only as the stake in that argument — first as the crowning glory of those sealed, then as the “deaths” of those not. Smith quotes D&C 132:13–14, 15–17, 19–25 through the address without ever using the words offspring or children of the exalted; his own 1954 answer to a member (jfs-agq-temple-marriage-1954) supplies “posterity,” and his 1951 conference address (jfs-continuation-of-seeds-1951) repeats the same verses with even less gloss.

title: Joseph Fielding Smith against the agitators: Adam presides, but “Christ is greater than Adam”
speaker: Joseph Fielding Smith
office: Of the Council of the Twelve Apostles; Church Historian and Recorder
venue: General conference, Saturday afternoon session (Conference Report, April 1942, pp. 25–28)

witnesses.scribe: Church History Library asset viewer, Conference Report, 112th Annual Conference (April 1942), pp. 25–28
witnesses.note: Official CHL scan of the printed Report; the Internet Archive item is a mirror of this scan. Image leaf = printed page + 1.

quotes.excerpt: I think we ought to get that clearly in our minds because there are those who are trying to stir up trouble among the Latter-day Saints today by teaching doctrines that are not in accordance with the revelations of the Lord, and maintaining that Authorities of the Church who have gone before taught doctrines which they did not teach. So we must have it understood clearly that while Adam will preside over his posterity as Michael, the prince, and as he will hold the keys of salvation, as he does, all of that will be under the direction of Jesus Christ, the Holy One of Israel, for Christ is greater than Adam.
quotes.note: A reframe performed in general conference on the nineteenth-century pulpit record itself. Smith does not argue that the Adam teaching is false; he argues that the earlier Authorities never taught it — “maintaining that Authorities of the Church who have gone before taught doctrines which they did not teach.” The occasion is the fundamentalist agitation of the period, and the resolution offered is hierarchical rather than historical: Adam holds the keys, under Christ, who is greater. Compare fp-repudiation-1865, where the correction is addressed to a text rather than to a claim about the record. The Adam question sits adjacent to this dataset's backward axis rather than inside it, so the quote is tagged only for the operation it performs, not for a position on the Father's origin — Smith says nothing here about that.

quotes.excerpt: And are priests of the Most High, after the order of Melchizedek, which was after the order of Enoch, which was after the order of the Only Begotten Son. Wherefore, as it is written, they are gods, even the sons of God — Wherefore, all things are theirs, whether life or death, or things present, or things to come, all are theirs and they are Christ's, and Christ is God's. (D. & C. 76:53-59)
quotes.note: Read aloud from D&C 76 with no gloss at the point of quotation — “they are gods, even the sons of God” passes without comment. Kept untagged because it is the revelation's language rather than Smith's claim; what he does with it is the next quote.

quotes.excerpt: What a wonderful thing it is to have the opportunity through the gospel of Jesus Christ of receiving all that the Father has, to become sons of God! Now they who enter into the terrestrial kingdom, and they who enter into the telestial kingdom will not be sons of God in the sense in which this term is used here. Of course we are all the children of God, every soul on the earth; we are His offspring, but in the great kingdom that shall be established in exaltation, all who receive exaltation will become sons of God, joint heirs with Jesus Christ and entitled to all the privileges and all the blessings of the Father's kingdom.
quotes.note: The gloss, delivered immediately after the verse, and it moves in one direction: the revelation's “they are gods” is restated three times as “sons of God,” “joint heirs,” and heirs to “all the privileges … of the Father's kingdom.” Nothing is denied and nothing generative is affirmed; the strongest word in the passage is the scripture's, and Smith's own vocabulary is inheritance language. Tagged FORWARD-EUPHEMISM on the same reading as hunter-exalted-man-1948-q4.

notes: Re-pulled verbatim from the Pulpit vault file talks/english/conference-reports/1942/1942-04-smith-salvation-and-exaltation-for-the-dead.md and checked against the djvu text of the Church History Library scan mirrored at the Internet Archive (conferencereport1942a, discourse at printed pp. 25–28, leaf n26); the scan's OCR reads “blessiags” for “blessings” and “all'” for “all” in the passages quoted, both corrected here to the printed reading. Conference Report, so A; historical-official. The printed Report supplies no formal title. The address is about temple work for the dead and the sealing chain — “each generation must be linked to the chain that goes before” — and the value of the entry is the pair of moves it makes in passing: a public reframe of what earlier Authorities taught (q1), and a reading of D&C 76's “they are gods” down into “sons of God, joint heirs” (q3), sixteen years before the Answers to Gospel Questions volumes in which the same author would handle the plurality question by mail (jfs-agq-plural-gods-1958).

title: George F. Richards: sealed couples “are to have an offspring, an eternal increase”
speaker: George F. Richards
office: Of the Council of the Twelve Apostles
venue: General priesthood session, Saturday evening (Conference Report, October 1942, p. 40)

witnesses.scribe: Church History Library asset viewer, Conference Report, 113th Semi-Annual Conference (October 1942), p. 40
witnesses.note: Official CHL scan of the printed Report; the Internet Archive item mirrors it. Image leaf = printed page + 1.

quotes.excerpt: Those who have attained those higher blessings, that is husband and wife sealed for time and eternity, they are to have an offspring, an eternal increase. It is unthinkable that that condition could be obtained outside of the marriage relations that the Lord hath ordained.
quotes.note: Offspring named, in the future tense, as a consequence of the sealing rather than a memory of mortality — which is more than most conference formulations of the period give. Still euphemism rather than explicit: “an offspring, an eternal increase” does not discriminate spirit children begotten hereafter from a sealed mortal posterity, which is exactly the ambiguity flagged at dew-2001. The second sentence is the argument the whole talk is built toward — the increase is unobtainable outside the ordained order, so the doctrine functions as the reason for the temple requirement.

notes: Re-pulled verbatim from the Pulpit vault file talks/english/conference-reports/1942/1942-10-richards-the-covenants-of-the-priesthood.md and checked word-for-word against the djvu text of the Church History Library scan mirrored at the Internet Archive (conferencereport1942sa, printed p. 40, leaf n41). Conference Report, so A; historical-official. The printed Report supplies no formal title; the vault's is supplied. Kept to one quote because the address is a short priesthood-covenant sermon and this is its only axis-bearing sentence: everything before it is the oath and covenant of the priesthood (“that all He has shall be given unto us”) and baptismal-covenant instruction. Richards was ordained an apostle in 1906 and was serving in the Council of the Twelve in October 1942 (he became President of the Quorum in 1945); he had also been Acting Patriarch to the Church until Joseph F. Smith's ordination as Patriarch at this same conference.

title: Joseph F. Merrill: half the couplet, and “leave mysteries alone”
speaker: Joseph F. Merrill
office: Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
venue: General conference, Saturday evening session (Conference Report, October 1943, pp. 84–87)

quotes.excerpt: Well, yes, we are going to live a long, long time, and many of the things, that we would like to know, we will have an opportunity to learn, when we pass beyond this sphere, if we are willing to comply with the conditions for advancement… Yet we are taught that “as God now is, man may become.” How may man become like God? By working, advancing, growing, increasing, by his efforts, and he will have a long, long time in which he can continue those efforts.
quotes.note: The half-couplet. Merrill quotes only the forward line, “as God now is, man may become,” and never the backward one; this is the standard mid-century citation habit and it is why couplet counts overstate how often the Father's past mortality was actually preached. Note also what the forward line is made to mean here: post-mortal *learning*, not offspring, not worlds, not godhood. The register is self-improvement.

quotes.excerpt: Now as to precept, I believe it is extremely important to confine our teaching to fundamentals. On this matter may I say I am strongly influenced, have been influenced for a considerable number of years, by the attitude of the late President A. W. Ivins. When we teach by precept, he said, we should confine our attention to things that are fundamental and leave mysteries alone.
quotes.note: Context rather than an independent claim, and deliberately not tagged RETREAT-REFRAME: Merrill's counsel is a general instruction to Church educators, not a ruling on this doctrine, and tagging it would be retrojection. It is recorded because of where it sits — an apostle who spent years as Church Commissioner of Education, telling teachers in the same address to stay on fundamentals and then reaching for the safe half of the couplet. Merrill defines a mystery procedurally: any passage on which informed readers disagree.

notes: Re-pulled verbatim from the Pulpit vault file talks/english/conference-reports/1943/1943-10-merrill-by-precept-and-example.md, transcribed from the Church History Library preservation scan of the printed Conference Report (Internet Archive conferencereport1943sa, printed pp. 85–87, leaf n86) with reading order reconstructed from the DjVu word coordinates; the file is status published. Conference Report, so A. Chosen over Merrill's April 1945 conference address (conferencereport1945a), which carries the same half-couplet — “a characteristic teaching of the Church is that ‘as God now is man may become’ — a statement in poetic language of our magnificent doctrine of eternal progression” — in a single sentence and nothing else; the 1943 address gives the same formula plus the mysteries counsel and the post-mortal-learning gloss, so it is the stronger of the two. Merrill's April 1944 address (“Man Inherits Attributes of God His Father”) is a third witness to the same theme and contains the striking “we are of the race of the Gods,” but no couplet; it is left out to avoid three near-identical Merrill entries. Note the delivery setting: an off-the-air session, spoken extemporaneously, which is why the doctrine appears as an aside.

title: John A. Widtsoe: “God” as a title describing an attainment — plurality without a chain
speaker: John A. Widtsoe
office: Member of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles and co-editor of the Improvement Era
venue: “Evidences and Reconciliations: LXXIII — Why Are the Words ‘God’ and ‘Father’ Applied to Several Personages?” Improvement Era 46, no. 12 (December 1943): 769

quotes.excerpt: It is evident, therefore, that since the Father, Son, and Holy Ghost are distinct personages, the word “God” is not only a name, but may be used also as a title describing an attainment or office. … In the same manner the title “God” may be applied to anyone who has attained to Godhood, that is, who has risen so high as to partake sufficiently of the essence of divinity.
quotes.note: The pivot of the whole column, and untagged because by itself it is a lexical claim rather than a doctrinal one: “God” is sometimes a name and sometimes a rank. Recorded because everything Widtsoe does with the plurality-of-gods material downstream depends on this distinction, and because the distinction is precisely what makes a regress unnecessary. If “god” is a rank, a plurality of gods is a fact about promoted creatures, not a fact about God's ancestry.

quotes.excerpt: This implies that many personages may have attained the power and place of Godhood. This does not make them in any sense coequal with God, or with his Son, or the Holy Ghost. Those who are denominated gods have a rank in the eternal councils, with corresponding power to help foster the purposes of the Father. There may be many generals in an earthly government, but only one commander-in-chief. Even so in the government of heaven.
quotes.note: Tagged RETREAT-REFRAME, and the tag is a judgment call that should be stated plainly rather than buried. Widtsoe is not declining a question and not denying a doctrine — he keeps the plurality of gods entirely. What he does is re-describe it as a hierarchy of rank under one commander-in-chief, which converts a doctrine that in Orson Pratt's and B. H. Roberts's hands generated an endless line of Gods into a static organizational chart with the Father permanently at the top. The reframing is the datum; a reader who thinks the category should be reserved for explicit retreats can discount the tag and keep the quote. Note also that the military analogy does the work an argument would otherwise have to do: it makes subordination feel obvious without ever addressing whether the commander-in-chief himself was once a general.

quotes.excerpt: The conditions under which Godhood may be attained have not been set forth fully. Necessarily so high a place can be obtained only by rigid obedience to God's laws. Those who aspire to such exaltation must be sealed as man and wife for time and eternity. Then they may continue the work of the Father in behalf of the waiting intelligences in the spirit world. Their “glory shall be a fulness and a continuation of the seeds forever and ever.”
quotes.note: The generative claim, delivered entirely in euphemism, which is why the tag is FORWARD-EUPHEMISM and not FORWARD-EXPLICIT. “Continue the work of the Father in behalf of the waiting intelligences” names no offspring and no mechanism; the only concrete word in the sentence is the D&C 132:19 quotation, and “a continuation of the seeds” is itself the scriptural euphemism. Compare widtsoe-exaltation-celestial-1948, where the same author writing five years later says flatly that “Spiritual children are begotten by them” — the same doctrine, one column stating it and one column gesturing at it, which is a useful measure of how much the plainness varies with the question being answered rather than with the era.

quotes.excerpt: The word “father” is also applied to different personages. God is the father of the spirits of all men. They were begotten spiritually by him in the pre-existent state. The relationship between God and man as father and son is real.
quotes.note: Untagged, and the restraint is the point. “Begotten spiritually by him” is begetting language, but it is unaccompanied: no mother, no gestation, no birth, and no organization-versus-begetting statement either, so it will not carry SPIRIT-BIRTH-VIVIPAROUS and will not carry SPIRIT-BIRTH-ADOPTION. Recorded as the mid-century default formula — real fatherhood asserted, mechanism unspecified — against which the explicit statements on both sides (fp-1909, jfs-agq-mother-in-heaven-1960 for viviparous; kfd-1844 for organization) should be read.

notes: Verified verbatim against the Internet Archive scan of the Improvement Era, December 1943 (item improvementera4612unse, IA leaf 34 = printed p. 769); the issue masthead confirms Volume 46, Number 12, and the contents page lists the piece as “Evidences and Reconciliations: LXXIII — Why Are the Words ‘God’ and ‘Father’ Applied to Several Personages? John A. Widtsoe 769.” Whitespace and line-break hyphenation from the OCR have been normalized in the excerpts; no words are changed. The column, not the book, is cited on purpose: “Evidences and Reconciliations” ran as a monthly numbered feature in the Era from the late 1930s and was only afterwards gathered into three Bookcraft volumes (1943, 1947, 1951) and then rearranged and retitled by G. Homer Durham for the one-volume 1960 edition, where this piece appears as “Why Are the Terms ‘God’ and ‘Father’ Applied to Several Personages?” The book texts are edited; the Era is the first printing and the form in which members actually read it. Correlation graded historical-official: the Improvement Era was the Church's official organ, its masthead named Widtsoe as an editor alongside the Church President, and Widtsoe was a sitting apostle answering doctrinal questions in it — but the column was never curriculum and the collected volumes were commercial. This is the cleanest single statement of the twentieth-century domestication of the plurality of gods, and it should be read against pratt-infinite-gods-1855 and roberts-endless-line-1895, which answer the same question by extending the series backwards, and against jfs-agq-plural-gods-1958, where Joseph Fielding Smith handles it a decade and a half later.

title: Stephen L Richards: eternal increase, mentioned “with a little hesitation”
speaker: Stephen L Richards
office: Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
venue: General conference, first day morning session (Conference Report, April 1945)

quotes.excerpt: …held out for those who attain exaltation which I mention to you with a little hesitation because I have not yet laid the foundation for it, and that is this: That these eternal homes of the future life shall be blessed with eternal increase so that families never cease growing in number, in virtue and power…
quotes.note: Increase named, and glossed as families “growing in number” — one step past the bare word but still short of naming spirit children or a mechanism, so FORWARD-EUPHEMISM rather than FORWARD-EXPLICIT. The self-conscious framing is the datum: an apostle in general conference flags the doctrine as something he mentions “with a little hesitation,” and justifies raising it only because a later argument depends on it. Compare the confidence of talmage-af-1899 (“the Church proclaims the eternal truth”) forty-six years earlier.

notes: Re-pulled verbatim from the Pulpit vault file talks/english/conference-reports/1945/1945-04-stephen-l-richards-teachings-of-the-church-set-forth-in-a-letter.md, transcribed from the Internet Archive scan of the printed Conference Report (conferencereport1945a, leaves 27–34) with reading order reconstructed from the DjVu XML. Conference Report, so A. The vault file is status draft and the surrounding paragraph carries two visible OCR artifacts (“p'romise”, “Creator of. the universe”); the excerpt is trimmed at both ends to a clean run and the elisions mark that trimming, not omitted argument — a maintainer should re-check this one against the page image before publication. The address is Richards reading and expounding a letter he had written setting out Church teachings for an enquirer, which is why the tone is expository. The passage stands two paragraphs after his statement that exaltation is “a never-ending experience in eternal progression and achievement,” and immediately before he tells the congregation that “much of this may seem highly theoretical and ethereal to you.”

title: Milton R. Hunter: “we are gods in embryo,” begotten of heavenly parents — with the couplet as the interpretive key
speaker: Milton R. Hunter
office: Of the First Council of the Seventy
venue: General priesthood meeting (Conference Report, October 1945)

quotes.excerpt: God has revealed to the Prophet Joseph Smith and to the other holy prophets that we are his children, the divine offspring of heavenly beings. Men and women in general are the greatest of God's creative work, being made in his own image, and endowed through inheritance from our heavenly parents with godly characteristics just as mortal children are endowed with the characteristics of their earthly parents. In other words, we are gods in embryo
quotes.note: “Gods in embryo,” argued from heredity: godly characteristics are inherited from heavenly parents the way mortal traits are inherited from earthly ones. The forward claim is real but unspecified — embryo of what activity is never said — so FORWARD-EUPHEMISM rather than FORWARD-EXPLICIT. HEAVENLY-MOTHER on the plural “heavenly parents,” per the reading at fp-1909-q1.

quotes.excerpt: Man, as a spirit, was begotten and born of heavenly parents, and reared to maturity in the eternal mansions of the Father prior to coming upon the earth in a temporal body to undergo an experience in mortality.
quotes.note: Read aloud in conference as “the following statement was made by President Joseph F. Smith.” The sentence is from the 1909 First Presidency statement “The Origin of Man” (see fp-1909), issued over Joseph F. Smith, John R. Winder, and Anthon H. Lund; Hunter attributes it to Smith personally and gives no citation, which is how a corporate First Presidency statement becomes a prophetic saying in the pulpit tradition. Begotten, born, and reared to maturity — the viviparous vocabulary intact.

quotes.excerpt: If one accepts that he is a son of God, in contrast to the concept that he is the offspring of an animal, he becomes impressed with the unlimited potential possibilities which are his. His eyes are turned heavenward instead of toward the ground. His hope is to become glorified — exalted — even like unto his heavenly parents.
quotes.note: The forward direction stated as a hope and framed against evolution — “in contrast to the concept that he is the offspring of an animal.” “Like unto his heavenly parents” is as far as it goes; parenthood is what the parents are called, not what the children are promised.

quotes.excerpt: The only way we can know God is to live as he lives, to think as he thinks, and to experience what he experiences. Interpreted in this light, we are brought face to face with the powerful Mormon doctrine which declares that “As man is God once was, and as God is man may be.”
quotes.note: The couplet quoted as “the powerful Mormon doctrine” under the side-head “The Way To Know God,” and put to epistemological work: knowing God requires experiencing what he experiences, therefore the couplet. Hunter's wording is a loose rendering of Snow's (“As man now is, God once was; as God now is, man may be”) — quoted here as printed. Tagged FATHER-MORTAL-EXPERIENCE only and referent ambiguous, per the snow-couplet precedent: the bare couplet settles neither the referent nor whether attainment as well as mortality is meant, and Hunter adds no gloss. Three years later the same speaker does add one (hunter-exalted-man-1948).

notes: Re-pulled verbatim from the Pulpit vault file talks/english/conference-reports/1945/1945-10-milton-r-hunter-the-purpose-of-life.md and checked word-for-word against the djvu text of the Church History Library preservation scan on the Internet Archive (conferencereport1945sa, leaves n107–n114). Conference Report, so A; historical-official. The printed Report supplies no formal title; the vault's “The Purpose of Life” is supplied from the printed index. Delivered in the priesthood meeting five weeks after the end of the war, and framed as a Latter-day Saint answer to the wartime cheapening of human life — the doctrine of divine parentage is offered as the ground of human dignity, which is worth noting because it is a use of the teaching, not merely a statement of it. This is the earliest of the Hunter conference addresses in the dataset and sets up the arc that follows: October 1947 (hunter-continuation-of-seeds-1947), October 1948 (hunter-exalted-man-1948), April 1949 (hunter-beget-spirit-children-1949), October 1949 (hunter-head-god-1949), April 1953 (hunter-eternal-life-defined-1953).

title: John A. Widtsoe reads Brigham Young in conference: “were he to do that he would cease to be exalted”
speaker: John A. Widtsoe
office: Of the Council of the Twelve Apostles
venue: General conference, second day morning session (Conference Report, April 1947, pp. 72–77)

witnesses.scribe: John A. Widtsoe, comp., Discourses of Brigham Young, p. 113 (Gospel Scholar Archive copy)
witnesses.note: Widtsoe's own topical compilation, printing the same paragraph under “Free Agency” and citing Journal of Discourses 11:272 — where the clause reads “he would cease to be God.”

witnesses.scribe: Journal of Discourses 11:272 (Gospel Scholar Archive copy)
witnesses.note: The underlying Brigham Young sermon as printed from Watt-era shorthand: “were he to do that, he would cease to be God.”

witnesses.scribe: Church History Catalog record, Conference Report, April 1947 (117th Annual Conference; call no. M205.1 C536)
witnesses.note: Authoritative catalog record for the printed Report; the Church's online conference archive does not reach back before 1971.

quotes.excerpt: The volition of the creature is free. This is a law of their existence, and the Lord cannot violate his own law. Were he to do that he would cease to be exalted. He has placed life and death before his children, and it is for them to choose.
quotes.note: Stance recorded as hedges, and the reason matters. This is not an assertion that God advances; it is the premise underneath the debate — that God is subject to a law he did not make and that his exalted standing is conditional on keeping it. A God who could “cease to be exalted” is not exalted by nature, which is as far toward the progression question as the sentence goes, and no further. Textual finding: the Journal of Discourses reading of this paragraph is “he would cease to be God” (JoD 11:272), and Widtsoe's own compilation Discourses of Brigham Young prints it that way on p. 113 — the substitution of “exalted” for “God” appears only here, in the printed Conference Report, from the compiler himself. Whether it is Widtsoe's pulpit paraphrase or a Report error cannot be settled from the printed record; either way, what a 1947 conference audience heard was a claim about God's exaltation rather than about his Godhood.

quotes.excerpt: I have never professed to be Brother Joseph, but only Brother Brigham, trying to do good to this people. I am no better nor any more important than any other man who is trying to do good. If I am, I do not know it. If I improve upon what the Lord has given me and continue to improve, I shall become like those who have gone before me. I shall be exalted in the Celestial Kingdom and be filled to overflowing with all the power I can wield, and all the keys and knowledge I can manage will be committed unto me.
quotes.note: Read under the side-head “Humility a Sign of Greatness,” which is what the passage is doing in the address — Widtsoe is illustrating Young's modesty, not teaching exaltation. The forward content is incidental and entirely in euphemism: exaltation, power, keys, knowledge. “Those who have gone before me” is deliberately not tagged INFINITE-CHAIN; in context it follows “I have never professed to be Brother Joseph,” and the predecessors in view are plainly the departed leaders, not a succession of Gods.

notes: Re-pulled verbatim from the Pulpit vault file talks/english/conference-reports/1947/1947-04-john-a-widtsoe-conference-address.md and checked word-for-word against the djvu text of the Church History Library preservation scan on the Internet Archive (conferencereport1947a, printed pp. 72–77, leaf n72). Conference Report, so A; historical-official; the printed Report supplies no formal title. The address is a pioneer-centennial tribute built almost entirely of Brigham Young quotations, and the Report prints no citation for any of them — a relay to weigh accordingly: what Young said reaches this pulpit through Watt-era shorthand and then through a topical compilation, and both quoted passages appear in Discourses of Brigham Young, which Widtsoe himself compiled. Entry-level hearsay is left at A because the Report is a faithful record of what Widtsoe said in 1947, which is the datum; the provenance of the Young material inside it is described here rather than overridden per quote, since both quotes share it. This is the same Widtsoe whose A Rational Theology supplies the progression paragraph Hugh B. Brown read in 1956 (brown-deify-man-1956, widtsoe-rational-theology-1915), and the same year as widtsoe-god-title-attainment-1943 and widtsoe-many-gods-1949 in the surrounding record.

title: Milton R. Hunter: the beget-spirit-children gloss, in brackets inside D&C 132
speaker: Milton R. Hunter
office: First Council of the Seventy
venue: General conference, second day afternoon session (Conference Report, October 1947, pp. 95–100)

witnesses.scribe: Church History Library catalog record, Conference Report, October 1947 (118th Semi-Annual Conference; call no. M204.1 A1 1880, 1897–)
witnesses.note: Authoritative catalog record for the printed Report; the Church's own online conference archive does not reach back before 1971.

quotes.excerpt: . . . and they shall pass by the angels, and the gods, which are set there, to their exaltation and glory in all things, as hath been sealed upon their heads, which glory shall be a fulness and a continuation of the seeds forever and ever. [And the Prophet Joseph Smith said that promise meant to have the power to beget spirit children.]
quotes.note: The bracket is printed in the Conference Report itself, inside Hunter's block quotation of D&C 132:19 and straddling the page break from p. 99 to p. 100 — verified on the scan. So the euphemism and its decoding are on the same printed line: the revelation says "a continuation of the seeds," and the Report's own square brackets say what that means. The spaced full stops at the head are the printed ellipsis of Hunter's quotation, not an editorial cut. Tagged FORWARD-EXPLICIT and not SPIRIT-BIRTH-VIVIPAROUS: "beget spirit children" names the offspring and the act but supplies no birth analogy and no physiology — that arrives eighteen months later in hunter-beget-spirit-children-1949 ("on the same principle as we were born to our Heavenly Parents"). Note also that the Joseph Smith attribution carries no citation, here or in 1949; the gloss is not in the King Follett Discourse, and no source is given for it either time.

quotes.excerpt: When the great judgment day comes, and when all men and women who have been true and faithful in all things stand before the judgment seat of God the Eternal Father and Jesus the Christ to give an account of their actions, words, and thoughts, while in mortality, it shall be said unto them, Well done my beloved servants, enter ye into your exaltation. Receive your life eternal.
quotes.note: The frame, kept because it shows what the address is: a talk to the youth of the Church about tobacco, liquor, and chastity, printed under the side-head "Blessings Promised to Righteous." The generative doctrine is the payoff of a Word of Wisdom sermon, which is where a good deal of the mid-century material actually lives.

quotes.excerpt: This is life eternal, my brothers and sisters. This is the exaltation which the gospel of Jesus Christ promises those who love God and keep his commandments.
quotes.note: The immediate closing gloss, and the whole euphemism problem in two sentences: having just printed "the power to beget spirit children" in brackets, Hunter re-covers it with the words "life eternal" and "exaltation." Whoever heard only the summary heard nothing generative at all.

notes: Verified word-for-word against the Church History Library preservation scan of the printed Conference Report on the Internet Archive (conferencereport1947sa, file conferencereport1181chur_djvu.txt, printed pp. 99–100; running head "Saturday, October 4 — Second Day"), and present in the Pulpit vault file talks/english/conference-reports/1947/1947-10-milton-r-hunter-conference-address.md, whose Final Review collated leaves n95–n100. Conference Report, so A; historical-official. The printed Report supplies no formal title. The OCR of the closing citation reads "(D. 6 C. 132:19-22.)" for "(D. & C. 132:19-22.)" and the excerpts above stop short of it. This entry completes a three-talk Milton R. Hunter arc that should be read in order, because the explicitness moves in one direction and then keeps moving: October 1947 (here) buries the decoding in square brackets inside a scripture block in a youth sermon; October 1948 (hunter-exalted-man-1948) reads the King Follett Discourse aloud and defines God as "an exalted man," while closing the forward direction in pure euphemism; April 1949 (hunter-beget-spirit-children-1949) states the whole package unbracketed — procreation, spirit children, the Eternal Mother, the birth analogy, and spirit infancy. Three general conferences in eighteen months, one member of the First Council of the Seventy, and the doctrine going from a bracket to a paragraph. It also further corrects the Pulpit lane's decade table, which recorded "spirit children" as rare before the 1960s: the phrase is in the printed Conference Report in its full generative sense in 1947, two years earlier than the dataset previously showed. The Joseph Smith gloss Hunter attributes without citation is sourced by Harold B. Lee in April 1957 (lee-children-after-resurrection-1957) to History of the Church 5:391-92, which Hunter's own 1953 wording paraphrases.

title: Bruce R. McConkie, early: the Father as one of “two glorified, exalted, resurrected beings”
speaker: Bruce R. McConkie
office: Of the First Council of the Seventy
venue: General conference, second day morning session (Conference Report, October 1947)

witnesses.scribe: Church History Catalog record, Conference Report, October 1947 (118th Semi-Annual Conference; call no. M204.1 A1 1880, 1897–)
witnesses.note: Authoritative catalog record for the printed Report; the Church's online conference archive does not reach back before 1971.

quotes.excerpt: There then appeared to him two glorified, exalted, resurrected beings — God the Eternal Father and Jesus Christ his Son — who, in answer to Joseph's question, told him that he should join none of them, for they were all wrong
quotes.note: The claim is carried by one adjective inside an appositive: the Father is a resurrected being, and resurrection is not a thing that happens to someone who has not died. That is an entailment of the word rather than an argument McConkie makes — he is retelling the First Vision and never returns to it — but it is a definite commitment, stated in general conference and printed in the Report, and it is what FATHER-MORTAL-EXPERIENCE is for. Referent father: the appositive names him. Nothing here about attainment, so FATHER-BECAME-GOD is not tagged; nothing here about a chain either.

quotes.excerpt: we do need to have in our hearts a fear that we may not make ourselves worthy, that we may not hew to the line of righteousness and keep the commandments of God with that degree of valiance which will give us our exaltation in the eternal worlds.
quotes.note: The forward direction in the same address, entirely in the standard formula: exaltation, eternal worlds, glory and honor added upon our heads. The contrast with q1 is the entry's point — a strong, unhedged descriptive claim about the Father's past, and nothing but euphemism about the hearers' future, in one twelve-minute sermon.

notes: Re-pulled verbatim from the Pulpit vault file talks/english/conference-reports/1947/1947-10-bruce-r-mcconkie-conference-address.md and checked word-for-word against the djvu text of the Church History Library preservation scan on the Internet Archive (conferencereport1947sa, file conferencereport1181chur_djvu.txt, leaves n59–n62); the em dashes around the appositive are the printed reading. Conference Report, so A; historical-official; the printed Report supplies no formal title. One of McConkie's earliest conference addresses — he had been called to the First Council of the Seventy in October 1946, and the corpus holds an earlier address from April 1947 — and its subject is not deity at all but the permanence of the kingdom and the reliability of the living oracles (“no man … can hold these keys of the kingdom of God and lead the people astray,” quoted from Wilford Woodruff). The Father's resurrection arrives as scenery. Worth reading against the later McConkie in the dataset: mcconkie-mormon-doctrine (1958), mcconkie-family-affair-1970, and mcconkie-heresies-1980, where the same author polices which parts of this cluster of teachings may be affirmed.

title: John A. Widtsoe: “Spiritual children are begotten by them”
speaker: John A. Widtsoe
office: Member of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles and co-editor of the Improvement Era
venue: “Evidences and Reconciliations: CXXI — How May Membership and Exaltation in the Celestial Kingdom Be Won?” Improvement Era 51, no. 3 (March 1948): 161, 189–190

witnesses.scribe: Improvement Era, March 1948, continuation pages
witnesses.note: The column runs from p. 161 and is concluded on pp. 189–190 under the running head EVIDENCES AND RECONCILIATIONS / (Concluded from page 189). The begetting sentence quoted below is on the continuation, not the opening page.

quotes.excerpt: It is a basic gospel doctrine that every person, except a very few, will be saved. It is an equally basic doctrine that salvation is graded. Every person will be placed in the hereafter according to his works.
quotes.note: The opening, recorded as context so the entry shows the frame Widtsoe is working in. The whole column is an exposition of D&C 76 and the three kingdoms; the generative claim in q2 arrives at the very end, as the last thing said about the highest of the three degrees of the highest kingdom, and it arrives without being asked for by the question at the head of the column.

quotes.excerpt: To enter the highest of these degrees in the celestial kingdom is to be exalted in the kingdom of God. Such exaltation comes to those who receive the higher ordinances of the Church, such as the temple endowment, and afterwards are sealed in marriage for time and eternity, whether on earth or in the hereafter. Those who are so sealed continue the family relationship eternally. Spiritual children are begotten by them. They carry on the work of salvation for the hosts of waiting spirits. They who are so exalted become even as the gods. They will be “from everlasting to everlasting, because they continue.”
quotes.note: FORWARD-EXPLICIT, and it clears the bar with room to spare: new spiritual children, begotten after this life, by exalted sealed couples, who thereby “become even as the gods.” Note the passive voice — “Spiritual children are begotten by them” — which keeps the sentence explicit about the fact while saying nothing about the physiology, so this is B2/B3 without B4 and carries no SPIRIT-BIRTH-VIVIPAROUS tag. Note also what Widtsoe conspicuously does not do with the symmetry he has just created: the exalted carry on “the work of salvation for the hosts of waiting spirits,” which is the Father's present work described as the destination of the faithful, and he draws no backward inference from it at all. The symmetry is an observation about the shape of the claim, recorded here rather than tagged.

notes: Verified verbatim against the Internet Archive scan of the Improvement Era, March 1948 (item improvementera5103unse); the opening is IA leaf 34 = printed p. 161, the concluding portion containing the begetting sentence is IA leaf 63 = printed pp. 189–190, and the contents page lists the piece as “Evidences and Reconciliations: CXXI — How May Membership and Exaltation in the Celestial Kingdom Be Won? John A. Widtsoe 161.” Whitespace and line-break hyphenation from the OCR have been normalized in the excerpts; no words are changed. Two scan artifacts disclosed so a re-checker does not think the text has been altered: the column opens with a decorative drop capital that the OCR reads as “Tt is a basic gospel doctrine,” restored here to “It”; and q2 runs across the p. 189 / p. 190 column break, so in the raw OCR reading order the sentence “Spiritual children are begotten by / them” is interrupted by an intervening advertisement. The two halves were verified separately against the scan and are quoted continuously. Cited to the Era column rather than to the collected Bookcraft volumes for the reasons given in widtsoe-god-title-attainment-1943; note that the 1960 Durham one-volume rearrangement prints this piece with the terrestrial glory compared to “the moon,” where the 1948 Era reads “as of the earth,” which is one more reason to quote the magazine. Correlation graded historical-official on the same basis as the 1943 column. Placement on the timeline: this sits between richards-eternal-increase-1945 and hunter-beget-spirit-children-1949 in a tight cluster of late-1940s General Authority statements that say the generative thing plainly, and it is the cleanest of them for the point that the claim was, at that moment, ordinary enough to appear as the closing paragraph of a general Q&A about the three degrees of glory rather than as a special topic. Read against widtsoe-god-title-attainment-1943, where the same author says the same thing in euphemism, and against the later retreat documented in hinckley-1997 and packer-parentage-1984.

title: Marion G. Romney: “I do not know the process”
speaker: Marion G. Romney
office: Assistant to the Council of the Twelve Apostles
venue: General conference, second day morning session (Conference Report, April 1948)

witnesses.scribe: Church History Library catalog record, Conference Report, April 1948 (118th Annual Conference)
witnesses.note: Authoritative CHL catalog record, call no. M204.1 A1 1880, 1897–, for the printed Conference Report. The vault treats this as canonical and the Internet Archive preservation scan conferencereport1948a as the page-by-page collation witness; the archive.org leaf anchor n76 is taken from the vault's own Final Review collation record.

quotes.excerpt: I believe he is the Father of my spirit and the Father of your spirit. I believe we were born to him and to our mother in heaven. I do not know the process, but I do know how we are born to our fathers and mothers in this earth and that is the way I think about it.
quotes.note: The most candid statement of the viviparous model in the twentieth-century pulpit corpus, precisely because it is offered as a personal working picture rather than as doctrine. Romney disclaims the mechanism in the same sentence in which he supplies it: the process is unknown, the earthly analogy is what he substitutes, and he says so. Tagged SPIRIT-BIRTH-VIVIPAROUS as stated, not implied — he does state that this is how he conceives it — with the hedge preserved here rather than in the tag. Compare pratt-seer and ballard-increase, where the same picture is asserted as physiology.

quotes.excerpt: I believe I was born to him as a spirit child in the spirit world before I was born here, and what I say about myself — and you will pardon the personal reference — I feel about every other human soul that lives in the earth. I believe we all lived with him before we came here.
quotes.note: The generalization: the personal testimony is immediately extended to every human being, which converts an autobiographical belief into a universal claim about origin without ever changing register.

quotes.excerpt: I have here in this book a talk upon which I have spent many hours in thought and preparation. I had intended to give it at this conference… I shall therefore not talk on that subject, but I will ask each of you, if you will, to offer a silent prayer in your heart for me… that I may have the Spirit of the Lord while I speak to you wholly extemporaneously.
quotes.note: Provenance, and it is load-bearing. Romney abandoned his prepared text because President David O. McKay had just given the same talk, and delivered this one unwritten. The Heavenly Mother passage is therefore unrehearsed — which is exactly why it is valuable evidence of the ambient mid-century understanding, and exactly why it should not be pressed as a considered doctrinal formulation.

notes: Re-pulled verbatim from the Pulpit vault file talks/english/conference-reports/1948/1948-04-marion-g-romney-conference-address.md, whose Final Review collated the body against the independent scan OCR conferencereport1948a, leaves n76–n79, at 0.9839 similarity with no vault change needed; the sole flagged span proved to be a running-head artifact in the scan's raw reading order rather than a vault error. Conference Report, so A; historical-official — the Church's online conference archive begins in 1971, so no hosted page exists. No hymn quotation appears, hence no citesId. This is the strongest single find in the 1925–1965 stretch: an Assistant to the Twelve, speaking extemporaneously in general conference, states spirit birth from a Mother in heaven and simultaneously admits the mechanism is unknown to him. Distinct from the 1964 Romney entry already in the dataset (see romney-1964) and from eldred-smith-no-increase-1948, which was delivered at the same conference era and takes the opposite line on divine progression.

title: Milton R. Hunter: “he is a man — an exalted man”, with all knowledge
speaker: Milton R. Hunter
office: First Council of the Seventy
venue: General conference, first day morning session (Conference Report, October 1948, pp. 13–18)

witnesses.scribe: Church History Library catalog record, Conference Report, October 1948 (call no. M204.1 A1 1880, 1897–)
witnesses.note: Authoritative catalog record for the printed Report; the Church's own online conference archive does not reach back before 1971.

quotes.excerpt: We believe that God is a personal being. By a personal being, we mean that he is a man — an exalted man. Approximately one hundred years ago, soon after Lorenzo Snow became a member of the true Church of Jesus Christ, he formulated a remarkable couplet which has since that time become famous. He said: “As man is, God once was; as God is, man may become.” (Lorenzo Snow, The Millennial Star 54:404.)
quotes.note: Both halves of the couplet, quoted in full, cited to a printed source, and used as the definition of what “personal being” means — not as an aside. “Exalted man” is attainment language, hence FATHER-BECAME-GOD; the couplet supplies the mortality, hence FATHER-MORTAL-EXPERIENCE as well. The referent is unambiguous because the whole address is about “God the Eternal Father… Elohim.”

quotes.excerpt: It is the first principle of the Gospel to know for a certainty the character of God, and to know that we may converse with him as one man converses with another, and that he was once a man like us; yea, that God himself, the Father of us all, dwelt on an earth, the same as Jesus Christ himself did. . . . … God himself was once as we are now, and is an exalted man, and sits enthroned in yonder heavens. That is the great secret.
quotes.note: Hunter reading the King Follett Discourse aloud in general conference in 1948, cited to Teachings of the Prophet Joseph Smith, pp. 345–346 (see kfd-1844). Two paragraphs of Hunter's block quotation, with a third between them omitted at the … (“I will go back to the beginning before the world was, to show what kind of a being God is…”); the spaced full stops inside the first paragraph are the printed ellipsis of Hunter's own quotation, not an editorial cut. Worth registering as a fact about the period: the King Follett material was not merely surviving in books in the 1940s, it was being read from the pulpit at general conference.

quotes.excerpt: We believe that God is omniscient: that he is all-knowing, that he sees all things and that he hears all sounds. In other words, that his sight and his hearing know no bounds, and that his knowledge is absolutely unlimited. …through his understanding of those laws and by putting them into operation he has created worlds without number, that is, they are not numbered to mortal man.
quotes.note: Denial, sitting in the same address as the strongest backward claim of the mid-century conference corpus — the cleanest single-speaker demonstration in this window that the two axes are independent. Hunter holds that the Father was once a man and progressed to godhood, and that his knowledge is now absolutely unlimited. MANY-WORLDS is earned by the neighbouring sentence in the same section, now carried inside the excerpt.

quotes.excerpt: I know that we will some day return to the presence of God our Eternal Father and become exalted, glorified, and celestialized beings, receiving a portion, along with him, of the great glory that he possesses.
quotes.note: The forward half as Hunter closes it — “a portion” of the Father's glory, alongside him. Compare his April 1949 address six months later (hunter-beget-spirit-children-1949), where the same speaker names the generative content outright. The two together show how much the explicitness varies within one man's conference preaching.

notes: Re-pulled verbatim from the Pulpit vault file talks/english/conference-reports/1948/1948-10-milton-r-hunter-conference-address.md, whose text was collated page-by-page against the Church History Library preservation scan on the Internet Archive (conferencereport1948sa, leaves n14–n19 = printed pp. 13–18) at 0.977 similarity, with one page-break paragraph split rejoined against the page image. Conference Report, so A. The printed Report supplies no formal title; the vault's is supplied from the discourse headings. This is the answer to the question the charter asked about Milton R. Hunter: his conference addresses do carry the exalted-man teaching, in almost the same words as the books that are not in the corpus, and he sources it to Snow and to the King Follett Discourse rather than presenting it as his own. Delivered as an explicit supplement to George F. Richards's address earlier the same session, which had covered the First Vision and the personality of Elohim.

title: Eldred G. Smith: in worlds without end shall have no increase
speaker: Eldred G. Smith
office: Patriarch to the Church
venue: General conference, second day afternoon session (Conference Report, October 1948)

witnesses.scribe: Church History Library catalog record, Conference Report, October 1948 (call no. M204.1 A1 1880, 1897–)
witnesses.note: Authoritative catalog record for the printed Report; the Church's own online conference archive does not reach back before 1971.

quotes.excerpt: We often say, and you have heard the expression as it has already been referred to in this conference, that “as man now is, God once was, and as God now is, man may become.” The only way man may become as God now is, is through fulfilling the laws of celestial marriage and the laws of the gospel, as I have just read to you the word of the Lord from the Doctrine and Covenants. Can we afford to overlook such opportunities for exaltation? Temple marriage is not just another form of church wedding; it is a divine covenant with the Lord that if we are faithful to the end, we may become as God now is.
quotes.note: The opening paragraph of the side-head “Opportunities for Exaltation,” which is also the side-head the previously recorded “no increase” paragraph sits under — this quote comes first in the discourse and is placed first here for that reason. Tagged FATHER-MORTAL-EXPERIENCE only, per the couplet precedent: the bare couplet fixes nothing about the referent, and Smith adds no gloss on its first half. Two things the surrounding sentences do state and the categories deliberately do not. First, “as it has already been referred to in this conference” — the couplet is treated as common conference currency in 1948, quoted from the pulpit without attribution, defence or hedge. Second, the mechanism: what Smith actually argues is that the only route to the couplet's second half is celestial marriage, which is what welds a cosmological claim to a temple-recommend exhortation. That weld is the entry's finding, and it is what makes the negative formulation in the next quote intelligible. Referent ambiguous, as with snow-couplet.

quotes.excerpt: Are you teaching your children to keep the Word of Wisdom only because it is a good health habit, or are you teaching them that by not keeping the Word of Wisdom they are not eligible to receive the knowledge and understanding to comprehend the laws of godliness, and so will be deprived of the opportunity to receive the power of the priesthood, and then not be permitted to enter the temple and thereby lose all the blessings of increase for all eternity? That is quite a price to pay, I would say. We are told they will become ministering angels, and in worlds without end shall have no increase. (See D. & C. 132:15-18.)
quotes.note: Eternal increase affirmed entirely by negation — the doctrine appears only as the thing the unworthy forfeit. Euphemism rather than explicit: “increase” is named and nothing else is, no offspring, no mechanism, no godhood. Note also the chain of consequence being drawn, from the Word of Wisdom through the temple to eternal increase, which is what puts a cosmological doctrine into a talk about parental teaching.

notes: Re-pulled verbatim from the Pulpit vault file talks/english/conference-reports/1948/1948-10-eldred-g-smith-conference-address.md, whose text was collated page-by-page against the Church History Library preservation scan on the Internet Archive (conferencereport1948sa, leaves n90–n94) at 0.983 similarity with no divergence beyond spacing and hyphenation. Conference Report, so A. The printed Report supplies no formal title; the vault's is supplied from the discourse headings. Both quotes stand under the single side-head “Opportunities for Exaltation” and are given here in discourse order, so quoteId q2 precedes q1 in the array; the ids are unchanged so that existing references still resolve. What this entry documents is a register shift rather than a new claim, and having both halves of the section makes the shift visible in one place: the full Snow couplet is quoted plainly and treated as conference commonplace, and then the doctrine it entails is preached in the negative, temple-marriage-incentive form — not “you will bear spirit children” but “they shall have no increase.” D&C 132:17 is cited, the entailment is intact, and the content has become an argument for a behavior, which is how a doctrine can remain formally in force while ceasing to be described. Entry-level referent moved from n/a to ambiguous now that the entry carries a backward-direction quote; per the snow-couplet ruling the bare couplet does not settle Father or Son, and Smith supplies nothing that would.

title: Milton R. Hunter: “the power to beget spirit children,” and our Eternal Mother
speaker: Milton R. Hunter
office: First Council of the Seventy
venue: General conference, second day morning session (Conference Report, April 1949)

witnesses.scribe: Church History Library catalog record, Conference Report, April 1949 (call no. M205.1 C536 v. 1–69, 1902–1970)
witnesses.note: Authoritative catalog record for the printed Report; the Internet Archive item conferencereport1949a is the Church History Library preservation scan the vault text was collated against.

quotes.excerpt: The Prophet Joseph Smith explained that this continuation of “the seeds” forever and ever, meant the power of procreation; in other words, the power to beget spirit children on the same principle as we were born to our Heavenly Parents, God the Eternal Father and our Eternal Mother. Therefore, a man cannot receive the highest exaltation without a woman, his wife, nor can a woman be exalted without her husband.
quotes.note: The whole package in two sentences, from the pulpit at general conference: increase glossed as procreation, the object named as spirit children, the mechanism named as “the same principle” by which we were born, and the Heavenly Mother named as a parent in the premortal birth. SPIRIT-BIRTH-VIVIPAROUS rather than adoption because the analogy Hunter draws is to birth, not to sealing. No backward claim about the Father's own origin is made, so the referent stays n/a: this is the forward direction only.

quotes.excerpt: …they shall pass by the angels and the gods, which are set there, to their exaltation and glory in all things, as hath been sealed upon their heads, which glory shall be a fulness and a continuation of the seeds forever and ever. Then shall they be gods.
quotes.note: D&C 132:19–20 as Hunter reads it (see dc-132), including the bracketed insertion “[and if they commit no sin to break that seal]” earlier in the verse, which is his. The revelation supplies the euphemism — “a continuation of the seeds” — and the quote above is Hunter supplying the referent for it. This is the pairing the whole dataset turns on: the scripture is opaque, the exposition is not.

quotes.excerpt: they were all sons and daughters of God the Eternal Father and our Eternal Mother in that celestial spirit realm before we came into mortality. We are taught that we were born into that spirit realm as babies, and that we grew to maturity there, undergoing the various experiences which were there for us prior to our coming to mortality.
quotes.note: Not merely birth but infancy and maturation — spirits “born into that spirit realm as babies” who “grew to maturity there.” That is the viviparous model carried past the moment of birth into a full developmental biography, which is further than the nineteenth-century sources usually go and further than anything the Church teaches now. Presented as catechesis: “We are taught.”

notes: Re-pulled verbatim from the Pulpit vault file talks/english/conference-reports/1949/1949-04-milton-r-hunter-conference-address.md, whose text was collated page-by-page against the Church History Library preservation scan on the Internet Archive (conferencereport1949a, leaves n65–n72); the file is status published. Conference Report, so A. The printed Report supplies no formal title. This is the strongest mid-century entry in the set and it corrects a gap in the frequency data: the Pulpit lane's decade table records “spirit children” as rare before the 1960s, but the phrase is here in 1949 in its full generative sense, not the modern sense of “we are God's spirit children.” Structurally the address is a survey of the degrees of glory; the passage sits under the side-head “Exaltation,” between the D&C 132:19–20 quotation and the D&C 132:17 quotation about angels who “cannot be enlarged” — so the affirmative statement and Eldred G. Smith's negative one (eldred-smith-no-increase-1948, eldred-smith-slavery-godhood-1950) are being preached from the same two verses in the same three-year stretch. Merged in v2 with the duplicate entry hunter-eternal-mother-1949, which recorded this same 4 April 1949 address under a second id with the same speaker, date, session, Conference Report pages, URL and vault file; the shared quote now appears once and the spirit-infancy passage is carried as q3. Hunter appears four times in the 1945–1949 conference corpus on this theme; this is the strongest and it supersedes the others — his October 1945 address (“Man, as a spirit, was begotten and born of heavenly parents… we are gods in embryo”) and his October 1949 remarks on Eternal Parents say less, in weaker language, than this one paragraph does. Together with romney-mother-in-heaven-1948 it shows that the mid-century quiet in the dataset is an artifact of collection, not of doctrine.

title: Milton R. Hunter: “the head God of all the Gods,” a Son who rose to Godhood, and a Father with many other kingdoms
speaker: Milton R. Hunter
office: Of the First Council of the Seventy
venue: General conference, second day morning session (Conference Report, October 1949)

witnesses.scribe: Church History Catalog record, Conference Report, October 1949 (120th Semi-Annual Conference; call no. M205.1 C536)
witnesses.note: Authoritative catalog record for the printed Report; the Church's online conference archive does not reach back before 1971.

quotes.excerpt: We accept, as Latter-day Saints, the teachings of the prophets to the effect that Jesus of Nazareth was the Only Begotten Son of the Eternal Father in the flesh; therefore, the revelation I referred to points back to a previous birth, a birth in the spirit world. You and I were sons and daughters of our Eternal Parents in the spirit world.
quotes.note: Spirit birth argued rather than asserted: because Christ is the Only Begotten “in the flesh,” the title Firstborn must point back to an earlier birth, and that birth is the one we all had. “Our Eternal Parents,” plural, carries HEAVENLY-MOTHER on the fp-1909 reading. Six months earlier the same speaker had spelled the mechanism out (hunter-beget-spirit-children-1949).

quotes.excerpt: During his pre-mortal life Jesus Christ rose to the status of Godhood. At that time he was foreordained to be the Savior of this world.
quotes.note: Godhood as a status reached, not held — and reached before mortality, which rules out the resurrection as the means. Referent son, on the precedent of snow-couplet-q3: the category tracks the claim that a divine person attained deity, and here the person is Christ. No mortality is in view, so FATHER-BECAME-GOD alone. Nothing is said about the Father's own origin anywhere in the address; the entry does not read the pattern backward for him.

quotes.excerpt: Joseph Smith tells us that at that grand council the head God of all the Gods called the council, and the purpose was to present a plan whereby his children were to come into mortal earth and have the experience of mortality and then return back into the presence of God.
quotes.note: Hunter's paraphrase of the King Follett Discourse (“the head of the Gods called a council of the Gods”), delivered without citation. Untagged deliberately: a head God presiding over a plurality of Gods is plurality with a hierarchy, not a succession, and the dataset treats those separately — compare pratt-key-theology-1855, whose “one Supreme Head” passages are likewise untagged. What it does show is that in 1949 the plural-Gods language of 1844 was still being repeated from the conference pulpit as ordinary narrative.

quotes.excerpt: There we would receive exaltation along with him, sharing with our Father and his Only Begotten Son all the same type of glory, power, honor, and happiness that they enjoy.
quotes.note: The forward promise in the strongest euphemistic register available — “all the same type of glory, power, honor, and happiness” — with no offspring and no mechanism. Same speaker, same year as the explicit April statement; the register is chosen sermon by sermon.

quotes.excerpt: The Father will say to his Only Begotten Son, “This is your world because of the great work that you did in being its Redeemer. You shall now be the Lord, you shall be the God, you shall be the king of this world forevermore. This is your kingdom.” Under the direction, then, of the Father who has many other kingdoms, Jesus Christ will preside here as your God and my God if we live worthy of celestial glory.
quotes.note: A plurality of worlds with a god assigned to each, staged as a speech the Father will make at the judgment. The subordinate clause is the load-bearing one — “the Father who has many other kingdoms” — and it makes this world one item in a portfolio. MANY-WORLDS takes no stance in the schema, being a framework rather than a position.

notes: Re-pulled verbatim from the Pulpit vault file talks/english/conference-reports/1949/1949-10-milton-r-hunter-conference-address.md and checked word-for-word against the djvu text of the Church History Library preservation scan on the Internet Archive (conferencereport1949sa, leaves n69–n75); the vault's “Latterday Saints” is a line-break artifact and the printed reading “Latter-day Saints” is used here. Conference Report, so A; historical-official; the printed Report supplies no formal title. The address is a testimony of the divinity of Christ that walks the whole plan from the grand council to the celestialized earth, which is why so much of the cosmology surfaces in passing. Entry-level referent is son because the one attainment-of-godhood claim in the address is about Christ; the Father appears only as the one who presides and assigns. Reads as the fourth stop in the Hunter arc — hunter-continuation-of-seeds-1947, hunter-exalted-man-1948, hunter-beget-spirit-children-1949, this, then hunter-eternal-life-defined-1953.

title: John A. Widtsoe answers “Are There Many Gods?” — and never mentions a chain
speaker: John A. Widtsoe
office: Member of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles and co-editor of the Improvement Era
venue: “Evidences and Reconciliations: CXL — Are There Many Gods?” Improvement Era 52, no. 12 (December 1949): 833, 864

witnesses.scribe: Improvement Era, December 1949, continuation page
witnesses.note: The column runs from p. 833 and is concluded on p. 864, where the closing answer quoted below appears.

quotes.excerpt: The Latter-day Saints believe in one supreme God. He is God, the Father, to whom we direct our prayers, in the name of Jesus, the Christ. Associated with the Father are his Son, Jesus the Christ, and the Holy Ghost. These three separate and distinct personages constitute the Godhead, the governing council of the universe.
quotes.note: The first sentence of an answer to the question “Are there many gods?” is “The Latter-day Saints believe in one supreme God.” Untagged, and recorded for the order: before Widtsoe concedes any plurality he establishes monotheistic priority, which is the shape of an apologetic reply rather than an exposition.

quotes.excerpt: This revealed doctrine of the composition and nature of the Godhead teaches that there are at least three Gods. … However, in the restored gospel the word god does not always refer to the governing council of the Gods; the Father, Son, and Holy Ghost. There are in the universe innumerable intelligent beings, some of whom have come to this earth. These beings, if faithful to the law of the Eternal Father, are steadily progressing toward his likeness. Those who have risen high in their progressive development are often spoken of as gods.
quotes.note: The concession and its immediate containment. Untagged: “progressing toward his likeness” and “often spoken of as gods” is theosis, which by itself is not evidence for generative exaltation and not evidence for a divine ancestry, and the whole point of this dataset is to refuse the slide. Note the two senses of “gods” Widtsoe is keeping apart — the Godhead's three, and the promoted many — and note that neither sense involves anyone standing behind the Father.

quotes.excerpt: While then, there are many gods there should nevertheless be a clear distinction between the Holy Trinity and those who because of righteous labors have won the title of gods. … The answer to the question at the head of this writing is that there are many gods.
quotes.note: The verdict, and the same reframing move as widtsoe-god-title-attainment-1943-q2, applied six years later to the question in its most direct form. The tag carries the same caveat: Widtsoe affirms the plurality outright — his last sentence is “there are many gods” — and what he reframes is its content, from a series that could extend in either direction into a two-tier arrangement of an unmoved Trinity above a promoted class. Also worth recording for its own sake: the bulk of the column between q2 and this verdict is spent defusing the Adam–God sermon, which tells you what the question “are there many gods?” had come to mean to Era readers by 1949.

notes: Verified verbatim against the Internet Archive scan of the Improvement Era, December 1949 (item improvementera5212unse); the opening is IA leaf 42 = printed p. 833, the conclusion is IA leaf 73 = printed p. 864, and the contents page lists the piece as “Evidences and Reconciliations: CXL — Are There Many Gods? John A. Widtsoe 833.” Whitespace and line-break hyphenation from the OCR have been normalized in the excerpts; no words are changed. One scan artifact disclosed: the column opens with a decorative drop capital that the OCR reads as “'T'he Latter-day Saints believe in one supreme God,” restored here to “The.” Cited to the Era rather than the collected volumes for the reasons given in widtsoe-god-title-attainment-1943; the 1960 Durham rearrangement prints this as chapter II.4 with the internal Brigham Young quotations from Discourses of Brigham Young dropped. Correlation graded historical-official on the same basis. This entry earns its place on the timeline by omission, and the omission should be stated rather than tagged. Asked flatly whether there are many gods, a sitting apostle in the Church's official magazine answers yes, cites Joseph Smith's plurality-of-gods sermon at length, cites D&C 76:58, 132:20, and 121:32, spends a third of the column disentangling Brigham Young's Adam sermon — and never once raises the question of whether the Father has a Father. Ninety-four years earlier Orson Pratt answered a version of the same question with an infinite series (pratt-infinite-gods-1855); fifty-four years earlier B. H. Roberts answered it with “an endless line of Gods, stretching back into the eternities” (roberts-endless-line-1895). By 1949 the same question produces a hierarchy chart. Read alongside jfs-agq-plural-gods-1958, where Joseph Fielding Smith fields the plurality question nine years later, and jfs-agq-as-man-is-1958, where he declines the backward question explicitly rather than simply passing it by.

title: Eldred G. Smith: the difference between slavery and godhood for eternity
speaker: Eldred G. Smith
office: Patriarch to the Church
venue: General conference, second day morning session (Conference Report, April 1950)

witnesses.scribe: Church History Library catalog record, Conference Report, April 1950 (call no. M204.1 A1 1880, 1897–)
witnesses.note: Authoritative catalog record for the printed Report; collated against the Church History Library preservation scan on the Internet Archive (conferencereport1950a, leaves n66–n71).

quotes.excerpt: I tell others, many of them, the difference between civil marriage and celestial or temple marriage is the difference between slavery and godhood for eternity. The Lord makes it sound a little nicer when he says those who reject the law of celestial marriage will be ministering angels, and worlds without end shall have no increase. Waiting on others with no further progress is an eternal existence but is not real living. Living involves progress.
quotes.note: Godhood named, and named as the stake in a marriage decision. The remarkable clause is the second one: “The Lord makes it sound a little nicer” is a speaker telling a general conference audience, in as many words, that the scriptural language is a softening of what he has just said plainly. Still FORWARD-EUPHEMISM and not FORWARD-EXPLICIT on this dataset's precedent — no offspring, no mechanism, nothing but the word “increase” doing the work (compare dc-132, where “then shall they be gods” is graded the same way).

notes: Re-pulled verbatim from the Pulpit vault file talks/english/conference-reports/1950/1950-04-smith-i-hope-the-lord-will-bless-me.md, whose text was collated page-by-page against the Church History Library preservation scan on the Internet Archive (conferencereport1950a); the file is status published. Conference Report, so A. The printed Report supplies no formal title; the vault's placeholder is taken from the opening line. Same speaker as eldred-smith-no-increase-1948, eighteen months later, in a talk that is otherwise entirely about teaching method, advertising, and Utah cigarette expenditure — the cosmological claim arrives as a sales argument for temple marriage, which is the register the mid-century material lives in. Note also that the October 1948 talk already carried the full Snow couplet (“We often say… that ‘as man now is, God once was, and as God now is, man may become’”) in a section headed “Opportunities for Exaltation”; that quote is not in the existing eldred-smith-no-increase-1948 entry and should be added to it rather than given an entry of its own.

title: Joseph Fielding Smith: “eternal lives” means the seeds continue — the same verses, ten years on, with less gloss
speaker: Joseph Fielding Smith
office: Of the Council of the Twelve Apostles; Church Historian and Recorder
venue: General conference, Sunday morning session (Conference Report, October 1951)

witnesses.scribe: Church History Library record, Conference Report, 122nd Semi-Annual Conference (October 1951)
witnesses.note: Authoritative catalog record for the printed Report.

quotes.excerpt: What does marriage mean to members of the Church? It means that they are receiving in that ordinance the greatest, the crowning blessing, the blessing of eternal lives. Now that's the way the Lord puts it, “eternal lives,” which means not only will the husband and the wife enter into eternal life, but their children who were born under the covenant likewise will be entitled through their faithfulness to eternal lives. And further, that the husband and the wife after the resurrection of the dead will not come to an end. By that the Lord means that they will have a continuation of the seeds forever, and the family organization does not come to an end.
quotes.note: The question is posed directly — “What does marriage mean to members of the Church?” — which is the moment a gloss would belong, and the answer is given in the revelation's own words. Note what “continuation of the seeds” is made to mean here: that the couple “will not come to an end,” i.e. endurance rather than generation. The children mentioned are the ones already “born under the covenant” in mortality, not children to come. Compare his own April 1941 address (jfs-the-deaths-1941), where the same verses are unpacked as eternal increase and its forfeiture.

quotes.excerpt: For these angels did not abide my law; therefore, they cannot be enlarged, but remain separately and singly, without exaltation, in their saved condition, to all eternity; and from henceforth are not gods, but are angels of God forever and ever. (D. & C. 132:16-17.) So the Lord says those of that class, who may be worthy to enter the kingdom of heaven, shall be like the angels, and they remain separately and singly in eternity.
quotes.note: D&C 132:16–17 quoted and then restated, and the restatement is the finding: the gloss keeps “separately and singly” and drops everything else, so the word increase never appears on the negative side of the ledger.
