In 1941 the same speaker glossed the neighbouring verse's “deaths” as “denied the privilege of eternal increase.” Untagged because the sentence Smith adds asserts nothing beyond the verse he has just read.

notes: Re-pulled verbatim from the Pulpit vault file talks/english/conference-reports/1951/1951-10-smith-with-the-help-of-the-lord-which.md and checked word-for-word against the djvu text of the Church History Library preservation scan on the Internet Archive (conferencereport1951sa, leaves n118–n122). Conference Report, so A; historical-official; the printed Report supplies no formal title. A temple-marriage and divorce sermon: the generative doctrine appears as the crowning blessing at stake in the covenant and then is left in the revelation's vocabulary, and the second half of the address is about broken sealings and children of divorce. Useful mostly as the middle term between jfs-the-deaths-1941 and jfs-agq-temple-marriage-1954 — the same apostle, the same verses, and the explicitness moving down and then back up depending on whether he is preaching or answering a member's letter.

title: Spencer W. Kimball: “eternal increase, perfection, and with it all — Godhood”
speaker: Spencer W. Kimball
office: Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
venue: General conference, Friday morning session (Conference Report, April 1952)

witnesses.scribe: Church History Library catalog record, Conference Report, April 1952 (call no. M204.1 A1 1880, 1897–)
witnesses.note: Authoritative catalog record for the printed Report; collated against the Church History Library preservation scan on the Internet Archive (conferencereport1952a, leaves n20–n25).

quotes.excerpt: The blessings of eternity contemplated in this “all” bring to men immortality and everlasting life, eternal growth, divine leadership, eternal increase, perfection, and with it all — Godhood.
quotes.note: The closing sentence of the address, and a list rather than an argument: increase is one item in a series terminating in Godhood, with the dash doing the emphasis. Nothing is defined — no offspring, no worlds, no mechanism — which is exactly the point of recording it. The “all” is from the parable of the prodigal son, “all that I have is thine,” which Kimball has spent the previous paragraphs on.

notes: Re-pulled verbatim from the Pulpit vault file talks/english/conference-reports/1952/1952-04-kimball-i-pray-for-the-spirit-of-the.md, whose text was collated page-by-page against the Church History Library preservation scan on the Internet Archive (conferencereport1952a); the file is status published. Conference Report, so A. The printed Report supplies no formal title; the vault's placeholder is taken from the opening line. Entered chiefly for the pairing with kimball-1976: the same man, twenty-four years apart, ends a conference address with “Godhood” in 1952 and warns the Church from the pulpit in 1976 against “the dissemination of doctrines which are not according to the scriptures and which are alleged to have been taught by some of the General Authorities of past generations.” The 1976 warning was aimed at Adam–God, not at this, and the entry should not be read as a retraction — but the register shift between the two is the kind of movement this timeline exists to show.

title: Milton R. Hunter defines eternal life: the power of eternal increase, and “children in the celestial glory”
speaker: Milton R. Hunter
office: Of the First Council of the Seventy
venue: General conference, Sunday morning session (Conference Report, April 1953)

quotes.excerpt: A careful study of the statements on this subject found in the scriptures, especially those found in the Doctrine and Covenants, reveals the fact that eternal life is the gift received by husband and wife who are married for eternity, and has reference to their power of eternal increase or a continuation of the seeds forever and ever. Also, exaltation may include less than a continuation of the seeds and Godhood may convey a slightly different shade of meaning.
quotes.note: A rare piece of lexical care from the pulpit: eternal life, exaltation, and Godhood are distinguished as three overlapping terms, with eternal life pinned to the sealed couple's power of increase and exaltation allowed to be something less. The distinction sharpens the euphemism problem rather than solving it — the word doing all the work, “increase,” is still undefined at this point in the address.

quotes.excerpt: The Prophet Joseph Smith points out that this “continuation of seeds forever and ever,” means to have children in the celestial glory.
quotes.note: The decoding, in a single sentence and this time unbracketed: children, in the celestial glory, after this life. FORWARD-EXPLICIT — offspring named and placed after the resurrection — but not SPIRIT-BIRTH-VIVIPAROUS, since no birth, physiology, or spirit-matter analogy is supplied here (contrast hunter-beget-spirit-children-1949). The Joseph Smith attribution is again given without a citation, as in 1947 and 1949; four years later Harold B. Lee reads the same gloss into conference and does cite it, to Documentary History of the Church 5:391–2 (lee-children-after-resurrection-1957), and Lee's text — “will continue to increase and have children in the celestial glory” — is close enough to Hunter's paraphrase to identify the source Hunter never named.

quotes.excerpt: A full knowledge of God can be attained only in the celestial degree of glory by those who ultimately become as he is. When one thinks as he thinks, acts as he acts, attains power comparable to that enjoyed by him, then that individual has attained exaltation or eternal life.
quotes.note: Hunter's answer to “how can we come to know God fully and completely,” and the closing register of the address: becoming as he is, glossed as thinking, acting, and power — not as parenthood. Whoever heard only this paragraph heard a doctrine of likeness; the generative content was two paragraphs earlier and one sentence long.

notes: Re-pulled verbatim from the Pulpit vault file talks/english/conference-reports/1953/1953-04-hunter-ftoday-the-hearts-of-millions-of-people.md and checked word-for-word against the djvu text of the Church History Library preservation scan on the Internet Archive (conferencereport1953a, leaves n75–n79). Conference Report, so A; historical-official; the printed Report supplies no formal title, and the vault filename preserves an OCR mangling of the opening drop-cap word (“Ftoday”). Delivered Easter Sunday morning, immediately after J. Reuben Clark's address on the resurrection, which is why the frame is immortality-versus-eternal-life from Moses 1:39: Hunter's structure is that immortality is universal and eternal life is the sealed couple's increase, and the whole doctrinal core sits in the middle of an Easter sermon. Fifth of the Hunter conference addresses in the dataset (1945, 1947, 1948, 1949 ×2, 1953).

title: Joseph Fielding Smith: “our Father had a Father and so on” — one page after “How God Does Not Progress”
speaker: Joseph Fielding Smith
office: President of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles and Church Historian (later President of the Church)
venue: Doctrines of Salvation, comp. Bruce R. McConkie (Salt Lake City: Bookcraft, 1954), vol. 1, ch. 1 “Character, Attributes, and Perfections of God”

quotes.excerpt: It seems very strange to me that members of the Church will hold to the doctrine, “God increases in knowledge as time goes on.”… But, how does anyone know? Where has the Lord ever revealed to us that he is lacking in knowledge? That he is still learning new truth; discovering new laws that are unknown to him? I think this kind of doctrine is very dangerous. I don't know where the Lord has ever declared such a thing. It is not contained in any revelation that I have read.
quotes.note: Denial. The section heading standing over this text is “HOW GOD DOES NOT PROGRESS,” and the paragraph heading is “FALSE NOTIONS ABOUT GOD'S PROGRESSION.” The unnamed “recently published article” he quotes and rejects is not identified in the book.

quotes.excerpt: The Prophet says: “If Jesus Christ was the Son of God, and John discovered that God the Father of Jesus Christ had a Father, you may suppose that he had a Father also.” Then he asks: “Where was there ever a son without a father? And where was there ever a father without first being a son?”
quotes.note: Smith quoting the Sermon in the Grove — see sermon-grove-1844 — and quoting the second question as well as the first, which is the one that makes the series unbounded in both directions at once.

quotes.excerpt: Yet we have to pass through mortality and receive the resurrection and then go on to perfection just as our Father did before us. The Prophet taught that our Father had a Father and so on. Is not this a reasonable thought, especially when we remember that the promises are made to us that we may become like him?
quotes.note: “And so on” is the whole regress in three words, and it is offered as “a reasonable thought” rather than as a mystery to be handled carefully — from the same author, in the same chapter, who calls belief in God's progression in knowledge dangerous.

notes: Verified by re-pulling the whole of chapter 1 and reading the section sequence in order: THE GODHEAD, MODERN KNOWLEDGE OF GOD, HOW GOD PROGRESSES, HOW GOD DOES NOT PROGRESS (with FALSE NOTIONS ABOUT GOD'S PROGRESSION, PERFECTION OF GOD NOT “RELATIVE,” SCRIPTURES PROVE OMNIPOTENCE OF GOD, GOD PROGRESSES BECAUSE OF KNOWLEDGE, WILL GOD DESTROY HIMSELF?), then HOW GOD IS EVERLASTING (with GOD IS AN EXALTED MAN and CHRIST BORN; YET FROM EVERLASTING), then HOW GOD IS FROM ETERNITY TO ETERNITY. The progression denial and the chain affirmation are separated by roughly a page of text and six intervening headings, so they are recorded here as separate quotes and must never be ellipsed together into one sentence, which is how the pair usually circulates. Taken together they are the cleanest single demonstration in this dataset that divine ancestry and divine progression are independent axes: Smith prints the chain approvingly a page after calling belief in God's continuing progression “very dangerous.” The chain half is expressly attributed to Joseph Smith and quotes both the Sermon in the Grove and the King Follett Discourse (see sermon-grove-1844 and kfd-1844). Graded never-official: Doctrines of Salvation is a Bookcraft compilation of Smith's sermons and writings assembled and captioned by Bruce R. McConkie, not a church publication, though it has long been treated as authoritative. The copy collated is a reflowed digital edition without the printed pagination, so sections are cited by heading; printed page numbers were not confirmed and are not asserted.

title: Joseph Fielding Smith: “Eternal lives means eternal increase—the continuation … of the seeds forever”
speaker: Joseph Fielding Smith
office: President of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles and Church Historian (later President of the Church)
venue: Answers to Gospel Questions, vol. 4 (1963), “The Importance of Temple Marriage” (question 39); answer given at the afternoon session of Ensign Stake conference, Assembly Hall, October 31, 1954

quotes.excerpt: Question: "What does a young woman or a young man do who marries outside of the temple of the Lord?"
quotes.note: A pastoral question from the floor of a stake conference, not a doctrinal one — which is why the answer is useful. The eternal-increase machinery gets stated not as speculation but as the reason a marriage licence matters, to an ordinary congregation.

quotes.excerpt: Those who are married in the temple for all time and eternity obtain the blessing of eternal lives. I put stress on eternal lives. Eternal life is God's life, that is, to be like him. Eternal lives means eternal increase—the continuation, as the revelation says, of the seeds forever.
quotes.note: The plural/singular distinction that carries the whole doctrine — “I put stress on eternal lives” — with “eternal increase” given as its definition. Graded euphemism because the content of “increase” is left in the D&C 132 idiom of seeds and continuation; no spirit offspring are named. See q2, where he does gloss it.

quotes.excerpt: Eternal deaths means that they are separately and singly forever. They have no increase. The Lord calls that death. They do not continue—that is, they do not continue through posterity—they come to an end.
quotes.note: The doctrine stated in the negative, which is where the euphemism gets unpacked: “they do not continue—that is, they do not continue through posterity.” Increase means posterity in eternity, in his own gloss, delivered as a warning rather than as a metaphysical claim. The affirmative version circulates constantly; this negative version is what gave it teeth in the mid-century Church.

notes: Verified by reading the complete answer — the question, HAVE NO CLAIM UPON EACH OTHER, INDIVIDUALS MAKE OWN CHOICE, WHERE DOES THE BLAME LIE?, IMPORTANCE OF TEMPLE MARRIAGE, THE PROBLEM OF DIVORCE — in the GSA copy. Provenance differs from the rest of this lane and is the reason for the exact date: the volume prints a parenthetical stating the answer was given at the afternoon session of Ensign Stake conference in the Assembly Hall on October 31, 1954, “as reported by Lola E. Meehan,” so this is a named reporter's transcript of a spoken answer rather than a written Improvement Era column, later gathered by Smith into volume 4 (published 1963). Graded hearsay A rather than C: unlike the Journal of Discourses shorthand, the text was selected and published by the speaker himself in a volume under his own name, but the reader should know a stenographer stands between the words and the page. Cited by title and volume sequence number (39); the reflowed digital edition carries no printed pagination and page numbers are not asserted. Correlation graded historical-official for the reasons given in jfs-agq-as-man-is-1958. Note the nine-year gap between utterance and book publication — a caution for anyone dating this lane by volume year alone.

title: Delbert L. Stapley: without the covenant, “without increase of posterity in the eternal world”
speaker: Delbert L. Stapley
office: Of the Council of the Twelve Apostles
venue: General conference, third day morning meeting (Conference Report, April 1955, pp. 65–68)

quotes.excerpt: Those who do not enter this order of the priesthood, that is, the eternal covenant of marriage, become angels of God in a separate and single state forever and ever, and thus are without increase of posterity in the eternal world; therefore without posterity they have no need of a kingdom.
quotes.note: Stapley's own words rather than a scripture quotation — he has just read D&C 131:1–4 and is explaining it before turning to D&C 132. The doctrine arrives by subtraction, as at eldred-smith-no-increase-1948 and pratt-celestial-marriage-1869: the unsealed are defined by the increase they lack. Euphemism rather than explicit, because “increase of posterity in the eternal world” does not distinguish spirit offspring begotten hereafter from a sealed mortal posterity. The last clause is the striking one — a kingdom is for a posterity to populate, so no posterity, no kingdom.

quotes.excerpt: Now, important as it might be to be appointed a ministering angel of God, certainly far more happiness would come to an individual to have at his side a loving companion, children, posterity — throughout the eternity, and unless we enter into this holy covenant of marriage and have it sealed by the Holy Spirit of promise, these blessings cannot be obtained by us.
quotes.note: The same contrast turned positive, and turned domestic: the alternative to angelhood is a companion and children “throughout the eternity.” This is the register in which mid-century conference audiences actually met the doctrine — not as cosmology but as the projection of a family into eternity. Compare mcconkie-family-affair-1970.

quotes.excerpt: This is the order and law of the Holy Priesthood. There is no other plan nor way to obtain eternal lives, and a continuation of posterity.
quotes.note: The summary formula near the close, joining “eternal lives” to “a continuation of posterity” — Stapley's substitution of posterity for the revelation's seeds, made three times in the address and never once unpacked into offspring or a mechanism.

notes: Re-pulled verbatim from the Pulpit vault file talks/english/conference-reports/1955/1955-04-stapley-days-of-the-prophet-of-god-who.md and checked word-for-word against the djvu text of the Church History Library preservation scan on the Internet Archive (conferencereport1955a, printed pp. 65–68, leaf n65). Conference Report, so A; historical-official; the printed Report supplies no formal title and the vault's filename and title are both artifacts of an earlier mis-split of this discourse from Marion D. Hanks's preceding address, since corrected in the corpus. The address is an exposition of the strait gate and the narrow way — gate as baptism, way as the temple ordinances — so the increase language functions as the terminus of a discipleship argument. It also quotes Brigham Young on the endowment and D&C 132:19–24 at length, including “Then shall they be gods, because they have no end,” with no gloss of any kind on the word gods.

title: Hugh B. Brown reads Widtsoe on God's growth, then draws the line: “deify man,” not humanize God
speaker: Hugh B. Brown
office: Assistant to the Council of the Twelve Apostles
venue: General conference, third day morning meeting (Conference Report, April 1956)

quotes.excerpt: In the beginning, which transcends our understanding, God undoubtedly exercised his will vigorously and thus gained great experience of the forces lying about him. As knowledge grew into greater knowledge by the persistent efforts of the will, his recognition of universal laws became greater until he obtained at last a conquest over the universe which to our finite understanding seems absolutely complete.
quotes.note: Brown reading John A. Widtsoe aloud in general conference (“On this point Dr. Widtsoe wrote as follows:”), from A Rational Theology — see widtsoe-rational-theology-1915. Every verb is completed: gained, grew, became, obtained at last. That makes it FATHER-BECAME-GOD, not DIVINE-PROGRESSION, on the same reading that separates talmage-conference-1915 from talmage-af-1899. Attainment language with no explicit mortality, so FATHER-BECAME-GOD alone. What Brown leaves out is the finding: Widtsoe's paragraph in A Rational Theology continues “if the great law of progression is accepted, God must have been engaged from the beginning, and must now be engaged in progressive development” — the present-tense clause, the one that actually asserts ongoing divine progression, does not survive into the 1956 pulpit relay. Two printed paragraphs are joined here with a space; nothing between them is omitted.

quotes.excerpt: If God is in fact our Father, then we, Father and children, belong to the same society of eternal intelligences. Among them he is supreme, he is the most advanced, most powerful, and most intelligent.
quotes.note: Context for the quote above and the one below, not tagged on its own. It is the ontology that makes the rest coherent — God and men as members of one society of co-eternal intelligences, differing by position on a scale — and it is argued from Abraham 3:22, 19, which Brown quotes immediately after. Naming God “the most advanced” of a class implies a scale he ascended, but Brown does not say so, and the no-retrojection rule keeps it out of the categories.

quotes.excerpt: When we say man may become like our Father, we do not mean to humanize God, but rather to deify man — not as he now is but as he may become. The difference between us is indescribably great, but it is one of degree rather than of kind.
quotes.note: The boundary drawn explicitly, six paragraphs after the Widtsoe reading and immediately after the Abraham 3 quotation: whatever the doctrine means, it does not mean bringing God down. The reframe and the claim are doing opposite work in the same breath — “degree rather than of kind” is the strong version of the teaching, and “we do not mean to humanize God” is the disclaimer attached to it. Compare packer-parentage-1984, where the same defensive move has hardened into a redefinition.

quotes.excerpt: To deny the possibility of eternal progression is to accept the awful alternative of eventual stagnation which would be damnation.
quotes.note: The stagnation argument, applied to man. B. H. Roberts had used the identical reasoning about God in 1911 — “an absolute immutability would require eternal immobility” (roberts-progress-of-god-1911) — and by 1956 it is being deployed for human progression only. Same argument, subject quietly changed.

notes: Re-pulled verbatim from the Pulpit vault file talks/english/conference-reports/1956/1956-04-brown-1-wonder-if-sometimes-our-people-think.md, transcribed from the Internet Archive scan of the printed Conference Report (conferencereport1956a, leaves n103–n106). Conference Report, so A. The vault file is status draft with an OCR-and-auto-clean provenance and no archive snapshot yet, and it records no calling; Brown was an Assistant to the Council of the Twelve in April 1956 (ordained an Apostle April 1958, First Presidency 1961), confirmed from the calling recorded on his other 1954–1956 conference files in the same corpus. The printed Report supplies no formal title. This entry replaces the Hugh B. Brown candidate Eugene England catalogues at BYU Studies 29/3 (1989), 44 — “when we speak of eternal increase we speak not only of increase of posterity, we speak of increase of knowledge…”, cited to Continuing the Quest (Deseret Press, 1961), 4. That book is in neither the Pulpit corpus nor the Gospel Scholar Archive, England's reproduction is unpunctuated lowercase OCR that cannot be quoted verbatim, and on inspection the passage is about *human* eternal increase (“increase of all that goes to make up godhood”) rather than God's progression, so it would have been mis-tagged as DIVINE-PROGRESSION had it been taken at England's framing. This address supplies verifiable Brown text on the same questions from the official record.

title: Antoine R. Ivins: “the privileges of eternal progress and eternal increase,” in a sermon on priesthood duty
speaker: Antoine R. Ivins
office: Of the First Council of the Seventy
venue: General conference, third day morning meeting (Conference Report, April 1956)

quotes.excerpt: for we have been told today that to attain to the highest exaltation in the kingdom of God, to sit with God in the councils of heaven, enjoying the privileges of eternal progress and eternal increase, that eventually at least we will have to learn to obey all of the commandments of God.
quotes.note: The whole of the doctrinal content, in the closing sentence of an otherwise administrative sermon about inactive Melchizedek Priesthood holders. Three formulas stacked without explanation — highest exaltation, sitting with God in the councils of heaven, eternal progress and eternal increase — and increase is once again the reward clause of an exhortation. Note “we have been told today”: Ivins is reporting the conference's own vocabulary back to it, which is what makes the sentence useful as a measure of how unremarkable the phrase had become by 1956.

notes: Re-pulled verbatim from the Pulpit vault file talks/english/conference-reports/1956/1956-04-ivins-my-beloved-brethren-and-sisters-it-is.md and checked word-for-word against the djvu text of the Church History Library–contributed scan on the Internet Archive (conferencereport1956a, leaves n100–n102). Conference Report, so A; historical-official; the printed Report supplies no formal title. Kept to one quote by design: this is a bare-formula talk, included because the dataset is comprehensive and because bare formulas are themselves the evidence for how the teaching travelled. The vault records Ivins's calling as “Seventy”; he served in the First Council of the Seventy from 1931 to 1967, which the address itself corroborates (“It is almost twenty-five years since I first faced a congregation in this capacity”). One scheduling detail worth recording, since the “we have been told today” could invite the wrong inference: Ivins is the twenty-third speaker of the meeting and Hugh B. Brown the twenty-fourth (brown-deify-man-1956, printed at leaf n103), so Brown's “deify man” address followed this one and cannot be its referent.

title: George Q. Morris: the Father's glorified state “comes through death and the resurrection”
speaker: George Q. Morris
office: Of the Council of the Twelve Apostles
venue: General conference, third day afternoon meeting (Conference Report, April 1956)

quotes.excerpt: And would we have an heaven without the principle of the atonement, would we ever have had an existence in heaven as spirit children of God without the atonement, for God the Eternal Father is a being, a Glorified Being of flesh and bone, exalted and celestialized, and that comes through death and the resurrection by means of the atonement.
quotes.note: The subject of the sentence is God the Eternal Father; the predicate is that he is glorified, exalted, and celestialized; and the trailing clause says that state “comes through death and the resurrection.” Read plainly it attributes to the Father both a death and an exaltation obtained through it — hence both FATHER-MORTAL-EXPERIENCE and FATHER-BECAME-GOD, per the precedent that mortality plus attainment takes both tags. The honest caveat, kept here rather than in the stance: the clause is grammatically loose, and “that comes through death and the resurrection” could be read as a general principle about how anyone becomes a glorified being of flesh and bone rather than as a biographical claim. On either reading the Father is the being it is predicated of, which is why the tags stand; but Morris is arguing about the necessity of the atonement, not narrating the Father's past, and he never returns to it. Compare hyde-once-a-child-1853 for the same claim made deliberately.

quotes.excerpt: Unless spirit and matter are inseparably connected, we cannot have a fulness of joy. And if they are so connected, we may have joy in its fullest degree, which I would say means attainment, achievement, exaltation. We must come to the earth; we must have earth life; we must go through death; and we must be exalted and glorified through the power of God and through the gospel and the resurrection.
quotes.note: The next two sentences, and they run the same sequence forward for the hearers that the previous sentence ran for the Father — earth life, death, exaltation, glory. The parallel is Morris's own, drawn in one breath and left unremarked; the categories record only what each sentence states, and the symmetry is noted here rather than tagged. Forward content itself is pure euphemism: attainment, achievement, exaltation.

notes: Re-pulled verbatim from the Pulpit vault file talks/english/conference-reports/1956/1956-04-morris-y-dear-brethren-and-sisters-i-have.md and checked word-for-word against the djvu text of the Church History Library–contributed scan on the Internet Archive (conferencereport1956a, leaves n111–n113); the capitalization of “Glorified Being” is the printed reading. Conference Report, so A; historical-official; the printed Report supplies no formal title, and the vault's filename preserves an OCR-mangled opening (“Y Dear Brethren” for “My dear brethren”). An atonement sermon given in the closing session, arguing that without the atonement there would have been no earth, no heaven, and no purpose to the spirit world — the claim about the Father arrives as the last link in that chain of counterfactuals. Morris was ordained an apostle in April 1954, two years before this address. Same conference and same day as brown-deify-man-1956 and ivins-eternal-progress-increase-1956, which were given in the morning meeting.

title: Harold B. Lee reads the Prophet's gloss into conference: “they will not have any children after the resurrection”
speaker: Harold B. Lee
office: Of the Council of the Twelve Apostles
venue: General conference, first day afternoon meeting (Conference Report, April 1957)

quotes.excerpt: In the celestial glory there are three heavens or degrees; And in order to obtain the highest, a man must enter into this order of the priesthood [meaning the new and everlasting covenant of marriage] ; And if he does not, he cannot obtain it. He may enter into the other, but that is the end of his kingdom; he cannot have an increase. (D & C 131:1-4.)
quotes.note: D&C 131:1–4 with the standard editorial bracket — which explains what the order of the priesthood is and says nothing about what the increase is. This is the verse as the century usually met it, and it is the setup for the gloss Lee is about to read.

quotes.excerpt: In explanation of that scripture, the Prophet Joseph Smith said this (and I read this because there seems to be some misunderstanding as to just what the Lord meant) the Prophet said in explanation:
quotes.note: The reason for the reading, stated aloud: there is “some misunderstanding as to just what the Lord meant.” An apostle telling a general conference that the revelation's own language has left the Saints unclear is direct evidence that the euphemism was not merely a modern reader's problem — and the remedy chosen is to read the plain gloss, not to restate it in his own words.

quotes.excerpt: Except a man and his wife enter into an everlasting covenant, and are married for eternity while in this probation, by the power and authority of the Holy Priesthood, they will cease to increase when they die; that is, they will not have any children after the resurrection. But those who are married by the power and authority of the priesthood in this life, and continue without committing the sin against the Holy Ghost, will continue to increase and have children in the celestial glory.
quotes.note: The gloss itself, cited to Documentary History of the Church 5:391–2 and read verbatim from the pulpit: increase means children, after the resurrection, in the celestial glory, and its absence means no children at all. FORWARD-EXPLICIT — offspring named and placed post-mortally — but not SPIRIT-BIRTH-VIVIPAROUS: the passage gives no mechanism, no gestation, and does not call the children spirits. The provenance is worth recording, since Milton R. Hunter had been paraphrasing this same Joseph Smith gloss in conference since 1947 with no citation attached (hunter-continuation-of-seeds-1947, hunter-beget-spirit-children-1949, hunter-eternal-life-defined-1953); Lee's citation supplies the source those addresses withheld, and Hunter's 1953 wording (“means to have children in the celestial glory”) is this text in paraphrase.

notes: Re-pulled verbatim from the Pulpit vault file talks/english/conference-reports/1957/1957-04-lee-this-morning-in-the-opening-session-our.md and checked word-for-word against the djvu text of the Church History Library–contributed scan on the Internet Archive (conferencereport1957a, leaves n20–n25); the space before the semicolon in “[meaning the new and everlasting covenant of marriage] ;” is the printed typesetting. Conference Report, so A; historical-official; the printed Report supplies no formal title. A temple-marriage sermon built from three watchman's stories at the temple gate house, then the scriptures, then the reasons young Latter-day Saints marry outside the temple — the doctrinal core is a single block in the middle, and everything around it is pastoral. Lee is expressly building on Bruce R. McConkie's address earlier in the same session, which quoted D&C 131:1–4 as well (the verse appears twice in this Report's record of the meeting). Also quotes Brigham Young from Journal of Discourses 10:24 on the first resurrection, and Orson F. Whitney's verse at the Alberta Temple.

title: Joseph Fielding Smith answers a member on the Snow couplet: “so far as the Father is concerned, we will leave that”
speaker: Joseph Fielding Smith
office: President of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles and Church Historian (later President of the Church)
venue: Answers to Gospel Questions, vol. 2 (1958), “As Man Is, God Once Was” (question 29); originally a “Your Question” column in the Improvement Era

quotes.excerpt: Question: "Will you kindly explain these two expressions, 'We know that there is a God in heaven, who is infinite and eternal, from everlasting to everlasting,' and 'As man is, God was; as God is man may become.' "
quotes.note: The question as a member actually asked it. Two things are data here: the member frames the couplet as sitting in tension with the Book of Mormon's “from everlasting to everlasting” God and asks for the two to be reconciled; and he misquotes the couplet, dropping “once” (“As man is, God was”). The question is what forces the answer below — Smith is not volunteering the topic.

quotes.excerpt: From this remark we gather that the Son was doing what the Father had done before him. However, so far as the Father is concerned, we will leave that until we receive further knowledge, when and if we become glorified in his kingdom. So we will deal with this subject in relation to the Son, Jesus Christ.
quotes.note: The decline, in one sentence, and it is the backward question specifically that is declined: a member asks what the couplet means about God, and the senior apostle brackets the Father entirely and redirects the whole answer onto Christ. Note the two moves are in adjacent clauses — “the Son was doing what the Father had done before him” quietly grants that the Father did something before, and the next clause refuses to say what. The concession is a gloss on John 5:19, which he quotes immediately above; it does not state mortality, and is not tagged as though it did.

quotes.excerpt: Now the Father has promised us, if we are obedient to his commandments, that we also shall advance line on line and precept on precept until we also may receive the fulness and become sons and daughters of God! If we become sons of God through obedience to the gospel, then we will be like him. Then he was as we are, we may become as he is, and this is good scripture.
quotes.note: Deliberately untagged. “Then he was as we are” is the couplet's backward half restated, but the antecedent of “he” is unrecoverable: the sentence opens with the Father promising and sits inside a section arguing from Christ as elder brother. Tagging this for the Father would be exactly the retrojection the couplet usually attracts. Recorded as context for the sentence it licenses in q3.

quotes.excerpt: From these and many other scriptures which have been revealed for our knowledge, obedience, and exaltation, we learn that Jesus Christ passed through all the vicissitudes, temptations, and trials of mortal life just as we have done. … Therefore, the caption heading this article must be true.
quotes.note: The reframe completed. Smith affirms the couplet — “the caption heading this article must be true” — but the demonstration he has just given is Christological, so the God who “once was” as man is here Christ, not the Father. Hence FATHER-MORTAL-EXPERIENCE carried with referent “son”: the category is the couplet's claim, and the referent records who Smith has attached it to. This is the era's authoritative way of keeping the couplet while refusing its usual subject.

notes: Verified by reading the complete Q&A (question, all four section headings — CHRIST IS OUR ELDER BROTHER, WE, TOO, MAY RECEIVE THE FULNESS, OTHER SCRIPTURAL EVIDENCE, THE SAVIOR PASSED THROUGH TRIALS OF MORTALITY — and the closing sentence) in the GSA copy of the collected five-volume edition. The column originated in Smith's monthly “Your Question” feature in the Improvement Era, which he had written since May 1953; this edition does not print the individual column dates, so the entry is dated by the publication year of volume 2 (1958) at year precision. The digital edition collated is reflowed and carries no printed pagination, so the Q&A is cited by its title and its sequence number within the volume (29) rather than by page; printed page numbers are not asserted. Correlation graded historical-official: the columns ran in the Church's official magazine and the books were issued by Deseret Book from the senior apostle, functioning as a semi-official doctrinal organ — though the 2012 Deseret Book reissue collated here carries a modern boilerplate disclaimer that the work “is not an official publication” of the Church, which is a 2012 legal notice and not a 1958 status. This is the cleanest BACKWARD-AGNOSTIC datum in the dataset from the mid-century Church, and it should be read against jfsmith-doctrines-salvation-1954, where the same author prints “The Prophet taught that our Father had a Father and so on” as “a reasonable thought.” Four years later, asked the question directly by a member, he declines to answer it. Neither text is his considered final word on the other; the pair is the point.

title: Joseph Fielding Smith reprints the Sermon in the Grove for a member — and the regress sentence is not in it
speaker: Joseph Fielding Smith
office: President of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles and Church Historian (later President of the Church)
venue: Answers to Gospel Questions, vol. 2 (1958), “Plural Gods” (question 32); originally a “Your Question” column in the Improvement Era

quotes.excerpt: Question: "In the book, 'Doctrines of Salvation,' Vol. 1, at the bottom of Page 11 and top of Page 12, we find a statement by the Prophet Joseph Smith about plural Gods. We also find in the Pearl of Great Price, Book of Moses, Chapter 1, Verse 6, the following: … These statements appear to be contradictory. Please explain this apparent contradiction."
quotes.note: The question as asked, and it is unusually well-aimed: the member has gone to Doctrines of Salvation 1:11–12 — the exact pages where Smith prints the Sermon in the Grove and the “our Father had a Father and so on” material — and set it against Moses 1:6, “there is no God besides me.” A lay reader in 1958 had located the tension precisely and asked the author of the book to resolve it. The leading “In” is given as “ln” in the scanned text and is corrected here as an OCR artifact.

quotes.excerpt: The apostles have discovered that there were Gods above, for Paul says God was the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ. I am bold to declare I have taught all the strong doctrines publicly, and always teach stronger doctrines in public than in private.
quotes.note: Joseph Smith, 16 June 1844, as Smith reproduces him from Teachings of the Prophet Joseph Smith, pp. 369–374 (see sermon-grove-1844). Marked implied and ambiguous deliberately: read in the full sermon “Gods above” opens the ascending series, but the sentence as printed here establishes only a God above Christ — the Father — because the elision described in the entry notes removes the line that makes the Father's own Father explicit. Tagging this as a clean statement of divine ancestry would import the missing sentence.

quotes.excerpt: It is perfectly true, as recorded in the Pearl of Great Price and in the Bible, that to us there is but one God. Correctly interpreted God in this sense means Godhead, for it is composed of Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. This Godhead presides over us, and to us, the inhabitants of this world, they constitute the only God, or Godhead. There is none other besides them. … However, as the Prophet has shown, there can be, and are, other Gods.
quotes.note: Smith's own resolution, in his own voice, and it is a jurisdictional one rather than a metaphysical one: Moses 1:6 is true of our jurisdiction, and other Gods exist outside it. Untagged because “other Gods” here is left undirected — the sentence does not say whether they stand above the Father, beside him, or after us — and the surrounding paragraphs point forward (exaltation) and sideways (other worlds), not backward.

quotes.excerpt: Thus the great universe of stars has multiplied beyond the comprehension of men. Evidently each of these great systems is governed by divine law; with divine presiding Gods, for it would be unreasonable to assume that each was not so governed.
quotes.note: The answer closes under the heading INNUMERABLE GALAXIES IN THE UNIVERSE. Smith puts the plurality of Gods into twentieth-century astronomy — a presiding God per galaxy — which distributes the plurality horizontally across worlds rather than vertically up a chain. That is the whole structural interest of this answer: given a question about Gods above, he supplies Gods alongside.

quotes.excerpt: Have we overlooked the fact that the scriptures, ancient and modern, hold out the promise to all those who are faithful and true to every covenant and obligation which the gospel places upon them that the reward will be that they shall become gods?
quotes.note: The forward direction stated without hedging, immediately before the D&C 132:20 quotation. Graded euphemism rather than explicit: “become gods” is deification language with no mention of spirit offspring here, so it is theosis and not by itself the generative claim.

notes: Verified by reading the complete Q&A (question, the block quotation of the Sermon in the Grove, and Smith's own sections TO US THERE IS ONE GODHEAD and INNUMERABLE GALAXIES IN THE UNIVERSE) in the GSA copy. The finding worth recording is an absence, and it is stated carefully. Smith reproduces roughly three pages of the Sermon in the Grove and marks an ellipsis immediately after “Away with him! Crucify him! Crucify him!” — the point in Teachings of the Prophet Joseph Smith, pp. 369–374 at which the sermon's best-known passage falls (“If Jesus Christ was the Son of God, and John discovered that God the Father of Jesus Christ had a Father, you may suppose that he had a Father also”). A full-text search of all five volumes for the phrase “had a Father” returns exactly one hit, and it is in the 1960 Mother in Heaven answer about our own Father, not this one; the regress sentence does not appear anywhere in the five volumes. Two readings are possible — Smith elided it, or the compiler did — and this entry asserts only that it is not in the reproduced text, not that Smith consciously suppressed it. Weigh it against jfsmith-doctrines-salvation-1954, where the same author prints that same regress approvingly, and against the member's question, which points at those very pages. Dated by publication year of volume 2 (1958) at year precision; this edition prints no individual column dates. Cited by title and volume sequence number (32); the reflowed digital edition carries no printed pagination and page numbers are not asserted. Correlation graded historical-official for the reasons given in jfs-agq-as-man-is-1958.

title: Eldred G. Smith: “We knew how our Heavenly Father came to his exaltation”
speaker: Eldred G. Smith
office: Patriarch to the Church
venue: General conference, first day afternoon meeting (Conference Report, April 1958)

quotes.excerpt: Every one of us came from a preearthly existence. We always existed.
quotes.note: Denial, on the abraham-3 and kfd-1844 reading: no beginning means no begetting. Two flat sentences at the head of the address, with no hedge and no attempt to reconcile them with the parentage claim that follows nine sentences later — see q2, where the same speaker calls us the children of heavenly parents. Holding both at once is the ordinary mid-century position rather than a contradiction he noticed; recorded here because the corpus needs the cases where the two models sit side by side in one voice.

quotes.excerpt: We are all children of our heavenly parents. We lived with them in the celestial kingdom. We walked by sight. We knew what the celestial glory was. As spirits only, we could not partake of the fulness thereof. We knew how our Heavenly Father came to his exaltation.
quotes.note: The last sentence is the datum. “Came to his exaltation” predicates an arrival on the Father — attainment language with no explicit mortality claim, which per the Father-status precedent is FATHER-BECAME-GOD alone, not FATHER-MORTAL-EXPERIENCE. And the epistemic frame is stronger than the claim: not merely that he came to it, but that we knew how, as a thing seen in the premortal celestial kingdom. Heavenly parents are asserted in the plural in the first sentence with no mechanism attached, so HEAVENLY-MOTHER without a spirit-birth tag, on the same reading as eldred-smith-spirit-offspring-1973-q1. Referent father for the tagged clause even though the parents are plural, since the category concerns the Father's status. Compare the same man fifteen years later (eldred-smith-spirit-offspring-1973), where the mortality half is stated as well: “the same type of experiences they had done.”

notes: Re-pulled verbatim from the Pulpit vault file talks/english/conference-reports/1958/1958-04-smith-i-pray-that-i-shall-have-an.md, whose body was collated against the Church History Library preservation scan of the printed Conference Report on the Internet Archive (conferencereport1958a, leaves n32–n34, similarity 0.9787 with no candidate diffs); the file is status published. Conference Report, so A. Transcription caveat: the vault's OCR ingest reflows the printed paragraphs, breaking the q2 passage across four lines; it is continuous prose on the printed page and is quoted here as such — no words are added, removed, or reordered. Distinct speaker-entry from eldred-smith-no-increase-1948 and eldred-smith-slavery-godhood-1950; the four Eldred G. Smith entries now in the corpus (1948, 1950, 1958, 1973) are worth reading as a set, since the same Patriarch to the Church supplies both the sharpest no-increase warning and the plainest statement that the Father arrived at his exaltation.

title: Antoine R. Ivins: “gods with the power of eternal increase” — that is the pearl of great price
speaker: Antoine R. Ivins
office: First Council of the Seventy
venue: General conference, second day morning meeting (Conference Report, April 1958)

quotes.excerpt: All that our Father hath shall be given to him who magnifies that calling, and that means that he shall take his wife to the temple, because we are told also that men who succeed in fully living up to all of the privileges and responsibilities of the Melchizedek Priesthood shall become gods with the power of eternal increase. That is the pearl of great price, brethren and sisters.
quotes.note: The payoff of an address built entirely on the oath and covenant of the priesthood (D&C 84:33–40, read aloud a few paragraphs earlier). Godhood and eternal increase are named together as the concrete content of “all that my Father hath” — but the attribution is a bare passive, “we are told,” with no source given, and nothing is said about offspring, worlds, or mechanism, so FORWARD-EUPHEMISM rather than FORWARD-EXPLICIT. What makes it worth recording is the placement: this is the definition of the sermon's controlling image, the pearl of great price, given to a general-conference congregation as the plain sense of temple marriage.

notes: Re-pulled verbatim from the Pulpit vault file talks/english/conference-reports/1958/1958-04-ivins-my-beloved-brethren-and-sisters-it-is.md, whose body was collated against the Church History Library preservation scan of the printed Conference Report on the Internet Archive (conferencereport1958a, leaves n49–n51, similarity 0.9671 with the two flagged candidates identified as running-head bleed in the scan rather than vault errors); the file is status published. Conference Report, so A. The printed Report supplies no title; the vault's placeholder is taken from the opening line. Ivins had earlier defined the image in his own voice — “The pearl of great price — what is it? It is the opportunity, I believe, to earn an exaltation in the kingdom of God” — and the tagged sentence is where that opportunity is cashed out as godhood plus increase. A lean entry by design: one sentence, one move.

title: Marion G. Romney, on the air to non-members: Joseph “referred to God as an ‘exalted man’”
speaker: Marion G. Romney
office: Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
venue: General conference, third day morning meeting (Conference Report, October 1958)

quotes.excerpt: In after years Joseph referred to God as an “exalted man,” and said that both he and the Son were personages of flesh and bone, as tangible as man.
quotes.note: King Follett compressed to two words and handed to a radio and television audience Romney has just addressed directly as “you who may not be members of the Church.” Marked implied because “exalted man” is adjectival: it states an attained condition without saying who exalted him, when, or from what — the same construction McConkie uses in Mormon Doctrine (“an exalted, glorified, and perfected Man”). Per the Father-status precedent, attainment language without explicit mortality is FATHER-BECAME-GOD alone. Romney supplies no gloss at all; the citation he attaches, D&C 130:22, covers only the flesh-and-bone half of the sentence, and the “exalted man” half is left standing on Joseph Smith's authority with no reference.

quotes.excerpt: Through subsequent revelations he learned that the relationship between God and men is that of parent and children. “The inhabitants” of the “worlds” … “are begotten sons and daughters unto God,” said the Lord to him in one of the revelations. (Ibid., 76:24.) The Prophet further learned through communication from heaven that as the begotten children of God we are endowed with the potential to become like him, even as mortal children may become like their mortal parents.
quotes.note: Untagged, and the reason is the same one that leaves romney-1964-q1 untagged: every clause is about children growing into likeness, and nothing here asserts that the exalted beget spirit children or supplies a mechanism. Two things are worth seeing anyway. First, this is the mortal-parents analogy that Romney will run again six years later in October 1964 — where he does place the Father inside the process (“through this process God himself attained perfection”), which is why that quote is tagged and this one is not. Second, MANY-WORLDS is deliberately withheld: the plural “worlds” survives inside the quotation of D&C 76:24 but carries no weight in Romney's argument, which is about parentage. The ellipsis inside the scripture quotation is Romney's own, as printed. The next sentence names “the doctrine of eternal progression” in a list of things Joseph learned and never defines it.

notes: Re-pulled verbatim from the Pulpit vault file talks/english/conference-reports/1958/1958-10-romney-my-beloved-brothers-and-sisters-and-friends.md, whose body was collated against the Church History Library preservation scan of the printed Conference Report on the Internet Archive (conferencereport1958sa, leaves n94–n97) and additionally read in full against the reconstructed page order; the final-review pass found no defects. Conference Report, so A. The register is the point of the entry: this is an explanatory address written for outsiders listening on radio and television, a genre in which the Church's more distinctive claims are usually softened, and the “exalted man” sentence goes out unhedged in the middle of it. Companion to romney-1964 and romney-mother-in-heaven-1948 — the same apostle across twenty years, hedging the Mother (“I do not know the process”), stating the Father's attainment plainly, and never once naming a chain.

title: George Q. Morris: “stripped of the greatest power, that of eternal increase”
speaker: George Q. Morris
office: Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
venue: General conference, second day morning meeting (Conference Report, October 1959)

quotes.excerpt: They may be saved in the celestial kingdom, but they cannot be enlarged, and forever and ever they remain a person of a lower degree — a lower order of being, stripped of the greatest power, that of eternal increase.
quotes.note: Morris's own voice, immediately after reading D&C 132:17 aloud — the verse says the unmarried “cannot be enlarged” and “are not gods, but are angels of God forever and ever,” and Morris supplies the gloss the verse does not: what they are stripped of is eternal increase, and increase is “the greatest power.” That identification is the reason the entry exists. It is still FORWARD-EUPHEMISM and not FORWARD-EXPLICIT: increase is ranked and named but never unpacked into offspring, spirit children, or worlds anywhere in the address.

quotes.excerpt: …and they shall pass by the angels, and the gods, which are set there, to their exaltation and glory in all things, as hath been sealed upon their heads, which glory shall be a fulness and a continuation of the seeds forever and ever. Then shall they be gods, because they have no end; therefore shall they be from everlasting to everlasting, because they continue; then shall they be above all, because all things are subject unto them. Then shall they be gods, because they have all power, and the angels are subject unto them.
quotes.note: D&C 132:19–20, read to the congregation at length and left entirely unglossed: Morris adds no comment on “a continuation of the seeds” and no comment on “then shall they be gods.” His only remark on the block is procedural — “Now I believe that our teachers, our leaders, and our parents must be taught and must teach these principles. They are as clear as words can make them, as the Lord has explained them.” Recorded per the unglossed-scripture rule, and tagged for what the quoted text says rather than for anything the speaker adds. The excerpt is trimmed at the front (elision marked) and joins the printed paragraph break between verses 19 and 20 without the intervening close-and-open quotation marks; no words are omitted there.

quotes.excerpt: He may enter into the other, but that is the end of his kingdom; he cannot have an increase.
quotes.note: The address closes on D&C 131:4, introduced as “a statement of the Prophet Joseph Smith,” again with no gloss. The negative formulation is the one that recurs across the mid-century conference corpus whenever increase is discussed without being described — compare eldred-smith-no-increase-1948. Between this and q2 the whole doctrine reaches the congregation in the Lord's words and Joseph's, with the apostle's single contribution being the ranking in q1.

notes: Re-pulled verbatim from the Pulpit vault file talks/english/conference-reports/1959/1959-10-morris-my-dear-brethren-and-sisters-i-am.md, whose body was collated against the Church History Library preservation scan of the printed Conference Report on the Internet Archive (conferencereport1959sa, leaves n47–n51) and read in full against the reconstructed page order; the pre-pass's low similarity score is accounted for by an adjacent speaker's running head that the vault correctly excludes, not by body drift. Conference Report, so A. The address is a sustained exposition of D&C 132 built as an answer to a youth-divorce statistic cited the day before by Mark E. Petersen, which is why its argument runs through the sealing power rather than through deification: increase enters as the thing the unsealed forfeit. citesId dc-132 for the block quotation.

title: Joseph Fielding Smith: “how did we become such, if we had no mother to give us spirit birth?”
speaker: Joseph Fielding Smith
office: President of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles and Church Historian (later President of the Church)
venue: Answers to Gospel Questions, vol. 3 (1960), “A Mother in Heaven” (question 35, beginning p. 142); originally a “Your Question” column in the Improvement Era

quotes.excerpt: Question: "Will you please give us the background of the 'theory' advanced of 'a Mother in Heaven'? Some feel that God is great enough to create spirits without any assistance, and if not, why then was not a Mother mentioned among the Godhead?"
quotes.note: The most revealing question in the five volumes. In 1960 a member could write to the senior apostle calling Heavenly Mother a “theory” — the scare quotes are the member's — and could offer, as the live alternative, that God made spirits unassisted. The objection is not modesty about her; it is doubt that she is needed. The answer below is shaped end to end by having to argue that she is.

quotes.excerpt: The fact that there is no reference to a mother in heaven either in the Bible, Book of Mormon or Doctrine and Covenants, is not sufficient proof that no such thing as a mother did exist there. If we had a Father, which we did, for all of these records speak of him, then does not good common sense tell us that we must have had a mother there also?
quotes.note: Conceded scriptural silence, answered from inference rather than revelation — “good common sense,” the same argument-form Brigham Young used in 1862. Conflation warning: this is one of three occurrences of the phrase “had a Father” on this page — the others being “We know that Jesus had a Father” and the section heading JESUS HAD A FATHER AND A MOTHER — and it is the only page in the five volumes where the phrase appears at all. Every occurrence is about our Father or Jesus' Father, not the Father's Father. It is not a regress statement and must not be quoted as one.

quotes.excerpt: If we are his offspring, then how did we become such, if we had no mother to give us spirit birth? … It is my turn to ask a question. How can we be the offspring of God, how can he be the Father of our spirits, unless we had a mother and were born?
quotes.note: Literal spirit birth asserted as the mechanism, and asserted as the reason a Mother must exist — the argument runs from the physiology to the person, not the reverse. “Spirit birth” and “were born” are unhedged. The section heading standing over this text is JESUS HAD A FATHER AND A MOTHER. Note the rhetorical turn: he answers the member's question with a question of his own.

quotes.excerpt: Their children will belong to them, and they will have the gift of "a fulness and a continuation of the seeds forever and ever. Then shall they be gods, because they have no end." … Now they will be blessed with the same blessings as those held by our Eternal Father—eternal increase.
quotes.note: The forward chain, and the reason this answer belongs on this timeline rather than only in a Heavenly Mother file: exalted couples receive posterity in eternity and become gods, and the blessing is identified as “the same blessings as those held by our Eternal Father.” The symmetry that produces — the Father presently exercising eternal increase, as we will — is an observation about the shape of the claim, not a backward assertion Smith makes, and is recorded here rather than tagged.

quotes.excerpt: Is it not feasible to believe that female spirits were created in the image of a "Mother in Heaven"?
quotes.note: The closing sentence of the answer, and a register datum: the whole case ends on “is it not feasible to believe,” with the phrase still inside quotation marks. Even the era's most confident defender of the doctrine leaves it at plausibility.

notes: Verified by reading the complete Q&A — question, the untitled opening, the section JESUS HAD A FATHER AND A MOTHER, and the closing Genesis 1:26–27 argument — in the GSA copy. Dated by publication year of volume 3 (1960) at year precision; this edition prints no individual column dates. The printed page anchor is derivable: at volume 4, question 38, Smith cross-references the immediately preceding answer in volume 3 as “‘Elias Is Noah,’ Answers to Gospel Questions, Vol. 3, pp. 138-41,” so “A Mother in Heaven,” which follows it directly, begins at p. 142. The end page is not derivable and is not asserted, and the reflowed digital edition carries no printed pagination of its own. Correlation graded historical-official for the reasons given in jfs-agq-as-man-is-1958. This is the mid-century link between snow-heavenly-mother-1885 / whitney-father-and-mother-1907 and the later hedged treatments (hinckley-daughters-of-god-1991, essay-2015): the doctrine is defended, the mechanism is literal, and the whole thing rests on common sense rather than revelation — which is precisely the vulnerability the later retreat exploits. Read against jfs-agq-personal-father-1966, where the same author, asked how a Father of flesh and bone produced spirit children, answers that “this question the Lord has not fully explained.”

title: Joseph Fielding Smith: “such questions should be ignored” — and Abraham's intelligences are begotten spirit children
speaker: Joseph Fielding Smith
office: President of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles and Church Historian (later President of the Church)
venue: Answers to Gospel Questions, vol. 3 (1960), “Why Does Not God Create Intelligence and Prevent Evil?” (question 30); originally a “Your Question” column in the Improvement Era

quotes.excerpt: Question: "If God is all powerful, why is he not able to create intelligence? In the Doctrine and Covenants, Section 93, verse 29, we read that 'intelligence or the light of truth was not created nor indeed can be.' If he is all powerful, why does he permit evil to rule in the world?"
quotes.note: A member pressing on the limits of divine power from D&C 93:29 — if something is uncreatable, in what sense is God omnipotent? The question presses on exactly the seam where uncreated intelligence meets a God who is himself situated in a series.

quotes.excerpt: Perhaps the time will not come while mortality endures that questions of this kind will not be propounded. The first thought that comes is that such questions should be ignored, but as they recur from time to time perhaps it is wisdom to answer them.
quotes.note: The bracketing move performed out loud, in the opening sentences of a column whose entire purpose is to answer members' questions. He answers only after recording that the first instinct was not to — and the stated reason for answering is recurrence, not merit. The same posture, applied to a different question, is what produces the decline in jfs-agq-as-man-is-1958.

quotes.excerpt: Why he cannot create intelligence is simply because intelligence, like time and space, always existed, and therefore did not have to be created. However, intelligences spoken of in the Book of Abraham were created, for these are spirit children of God, begotten sons.
quotes.note: A distinction that matters for the tripartite question and is easily missed: singular “intelligence” (D&C 93:29) is uncreated and co-eternal, while the plural “intelligences” of Abraham 3:22 are not a third pre-spirit tier at all — Smith collapses them into the begotten spirit children. On this reading the framework is two-stage (uncreated intelligence, then begetting as spirit), not the three-stage scheme B. H. Roberts and others built from the same verse; compare bh-roberts-tripartite and madsen-eternal-man-1966. “Begotten sons” is begetting language, but no physiology is stated here, so no spirit-birth category is applied — for that from the same author see jfs-agq-mother-in-heaven-1960.

notes: Verified by reading the complete Q&A — question, the section INTELLIGENCE CO-ETERNAL WITH GOD, and the second half on free agency (OPPOSITION NECESSARY, GOD IS NOT LIMITED BY JUSTICE) — in the GSA copy. Dated by publication year of volume 3 (1960) at year precision; this edition prints no individual column dates. Cited by title and volume sequence number (30); the reflowed digital edition carries no printed pagination and page numbers are not asserted. Correlation graded historical-official for the reasons given in jfs-agq-as-man-is-1958. Carried as sourceType original with citesId to abraham-3 because the value here is Smith's own reading of Abraham 3:22, not the quotation of it. Read alongside jfs-agq-intelligences-1963, where he takes the opposite tack on the same verse and declares the nature of an intelligence unknowable.

title: Delbert L. Stapley: joint-heirship as ascent “to the station of Godhood”
speaker: Delbert L. Stapley
office: Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
venue: General conference, second day afternoon meeting (Conference Report, April 1961)

quotes.excerpt: In the important doctrinal discourse known as the “King Follett Sermon” the Prophet Joseph Smith, referring to those who “shall be heirs of God and jointheirs with Jesus Christ,” described jointheirship as inheriting the same power, the same glory, and the same exaltation, until an individual ascends to the station of Godhood and rises to the throne of eternal power, sharing the rewards with all the faithful who have preceded him.
quotes.note: Paraphrase, not quotation — Stapley reports what King Follett “described” rather than reading it — and the paraphrase is the datum. What he takes from the sermon is the forward half only: joint-heirs ascend to Godhood. The sermon's backward half, God himself once as we are now, is not mentioned here or anywhere else in the address, though the sermon is named outright and treated as an authority. Untagged, because ascent to Godhood is theosis and nothing more; the entry's tagged claim is in q2.

quotes.excerpt: The everlasting covenant of marriage, ordained of God for man and woman, also is to be entered into and the marriage contract sealed eternally by the authority of the Holy Priesthood of God. Otherwise, the highest degree of the celestial kingdom cannot be attained nor Godhood acquired, which exalted condition assures continuation of the lives forever.
quotes.note: Godhood made conditional on eternal marriage, with “continuation of the lives” — the phrase of D&C 132:22, used without attribution — as what the exalted condition assures. Euphemism rather than explicit: the phrase is the standard veil over posterity, and Stapley never lifts it. Two paragraphs earlier he had stated the premise in the barest possible form, “To become like God we must possess the powers of Godhood,” and then listed the ordinances that convey them — endowment first, then this. Elsewhere in the address he quotes D&C 132:37 (Abraham, Isaac and Jacob “are not angels but are Gods”) and D&C 76:55–59 (“they are gods, even the sons of God”), both without gloss.

notes: Re-pulled verbatim from the Pulpit vault file talks/english/conference-reports/1961/1961-04-stapley-my-brothers-and-sisters-as-i-contemplate.md, whose body was collated against the Church History Library preservation scan of the printed Conference Report on the Internet Archive (conferencereport1961a, leaves n65–n69) with the low-similarity leaf checked directly against the BookReader page images; the final-review pass removed three running-head bleeds and confirmed the printed typo “purfied” in the D&C 50:29 quotation as genuine. Conference Report, so A. The address is a joint-heirship sermon in the legal register — Stapley works from the law of equity and the idea that “a joint-heir legally inherits and shares all equities and gifts in equal interest,” which is what makes the Godhood conclusion feel deduced rather than asserted. citesId kfd-1844 for the named paraphrase.

title: Henry D. Taylor: the hymn's closing prayer, mid-century
speaker: Henry D. Taylor
office: Assistant to the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
venue: General conference, third day morning meeting (Conference Report, October 1961)

quotes.excerpt: We sing a beautiful hymn that is a favorite of mine. It refers to our existence prior to coming to this earth. Sister Eliza R. Snow, the author, poses some very meaningful questions, and in addressing our Father in heaven asks:
quotes.note: The framing, and the reframing. Taylor tells the congregation what the hymn is about — premortal existence — and the Mother is not named in the summary even though she is named in the stanza he is about to read. This is the mid-century handling in miniature: the text is preserved intact and its most distinctive claim is quietly not the point.

quotes.excerpt: "When I leave this frail existence; When I lay this mortal by, Father, Mother, may I meet you In your royal courts on high? Then at length, when I've completed All you sent me forth to do; With your mutual approbation, Let me come and dwell with you." ("O My Father")
quotes.note: The Mother addressed directly, in general conference, in 1961. Punctuation follows the Conference Report printing, which uses semicolons where the hymnal has commas. Taylor attributes the hymn by title. See o-my-father.

notes: Re-pulled verbatim from the Pulpit vault file talks/english/conference-reports/1961/1961-10-taylor-we-sing-a-beautiful-hymn-that-is.md, whose Final Review collated §0 against conferencereport1961sa, leaves n101–n103, removing two running-head bleeds mid-sentence and making no other body change; the heavyweight pass rebuilt the report's reading order from the scan's DjVu word coordinates and corrected the date and session from the report's own dateline. The vault-supplied title is the talk's opening words, since the printed Report gives none. Conference Report, so A; historical-official — the Church's online archive begins in 1971. A citation and nothing more: Taylor quotes the hymn to introduce a sermon about keeping all the commandments, illustrated by the blind men and the elephant, and never returns to the Mother. It is filed anyway because it is the only located general conference witness to the hymn's Heavenly Mother stanzas in the whole of the 1950s and early 1960s, and because the shape of the citation — full stanza, correct attribution, no comment — is itself the finding for that decade.

title: Joseph Fielding Smith declines a member's man-to-God analogy: “we need not bother about the mysteries”
speaker: Joseph Fielding Smith
office: President of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles and Church Historian (later President of the Church)
venue: Answers to Gospel Questions, vol. 4 (1963), “Intelligences and Eternal Life” (question 24); originally a “Your Question” column in the Improvement Era

quotes.excerpt: Question: "… while 'intelligences' were neither made nor created and therefore cannot be destroyed, I have wondered why animals were created for this life only. Is not the difference between man and animals a matter of degree of intelligence, just as the difference between man and God is? Why then should animals be for this life only?"
quotes.note: The question that makes this entry worth keeping. The member states, as something the Church has taught him, that the difference between man and God is one of degree and not of kind — and states it in passing, as an uncontroversial premise on the way to asking about animals. That is how thoroughly the ladder cosmology had been absorbed by ordinary members by 1963.

quotes.excerpt: Some of our writers have endeavored to explain what an intelligence is, but to do so is futile, for we have never been given any insight into this matter beyond what the Lord has fragmentarily revealed. We know, however, that there is something called intelligence which always existed. It is the real eternal part of man, which was not created nor made. This intelligence combined with the spirit constitutes a spiritual identity or individual.
quotes.note: “Some of our writers” is a swipe at the tripartite theorists — B. H. Roberts and his successors — without naming them; compare bh-roberts-tripartite and madsen-eternal-man-1966. What he retains is thinner than what he rejects: an uncreated something combined with spirit, with the combining left unexplained. Note the drift from his 1960 answer (jfs-agq-create-intelligence-1960), where he was willing to say what Abraham's intelligences were.

quotes.excerpt: There are so many things in the gospel which are essential for us to know and observe, that we need not bother about the mysteries which have never been revealed. There are many things that we will know when we receive the resurrection and attain to the glories of the kingdom of our Eternal Father, which we cannot understand in this mortal state even if they were revealed to us.
quotes.note: The mysteries-are-not-your-business reframe, in the mid-century idiom. Its force here is what it silently covers: the member's premise that man differs from God in degree is never engaged, endorsed, or corrected anywhere in the answer. The analogy that would license the whole ladder simply drops.

notes: Verified by reading the complete Q&A — the full question (abridged in the excerpt above with an ellipsis at the front; the member also rehearses D&C 76:24, Acts 17, and Moses on the creation of animals), the section “MAN WAS ALSO IN THE BEGINNING WITH GOD,” ALMA'S WORDS TO ZEEZROM, and the second half on the resurrection of animals — in the GSA copy. Dated by publication year of volume 4 (1963) at year precision; this edition prints no individual column dates. Cited by title and volume sequence number (24); the reflowed digital edition carries no printed pagination and page numbers are not asserted. Correlation graded historical-official for the reasons given in jfs-agq-as-man-is-1958. Smith quotes his own earlier book The Progress of Man, p. 11, inside the answer. The pattern this entry documents with jfs-agq-as-man-is-1958 and jfs-agq-personal-father-1966 is consistent across the lane: members supply the speculative frame, and the senior apostle answers the tractable half of the question and lets the frame pass in silence.

title: Marion G. Romney: a process infinitely repeated in nature
speaker: Marion G. Romney
office: Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
venue: General conference, Saturday morning session (Conference Report, October 1964)

quotes.excerpt: We all know that like begets like and that for the offspring to grow to the stature of his parent is a process infinitely repeated in nature. We can therefore understand that for a son of God to grow to the likeness of his Father in heaven is in harmony with natural law. We see this law demonstrated every few years in our own experience. Sons born to mortal fathers grow up to be like their fathers in the flesh. This is the way it will be with spirit sons of God. They will grow up to be like their Father in heaven. Joseph taught this obvious truth.
quotes.note: Spirit sons of God growing to the stature of their parent, argued from natural law. Untagged: every clause is about growth into likeness, and nothing in it asserts that the exalted beget spirit children or supplies a mechanism — the generative reading is supplied by the reader, not by Romney.

quotes.excerpt: As a matter of fact, he taught that through this process God himself attained perfection. From President Snow's understanding of the teachings of the Prophet on this doctrinal point, he coined the familiar couplet: “As man is, God once was; as God is, man may become.” This teaching is peculiar to the restored gospel of Jesus Christ.
quotes.note: “This process” is the one just called “infinitely repeated in nature,” with the Father placed inside it — a chain is implicit by symmetry, but per the no-retrojection principle it is not tagged INFINITE-CHAIN: Romney never states the backward direction. “God himself attained perfection” is the clearest FATHER-BECAME-GOD statement in the set.

notes: The only located instance in the twentieth-century conference corpus (~10,000 addresses, 1897–1970 plus the modern era) where the parent-offspring mechanism is called infinitely repeated and God Himself is placed within it. Verified against the Internet Archive scan of the October 1964 Conference Report. Collated against the Internet Archive scan conferencereport1964sa at leaf n50 (running head “Saturday, October 3”); title page gives the conference dates as October 2, 3, 4, 1964.

title: Joseph Fielding Smith: contraception and “the blessings of eternal increase”
speaker: Joseph Fielding Smith
office: President of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
venue: General conference, first day afternoon meeting (Conference Report, October 1965)

quotes.excerpt: If the love of the world and the wicked practices of the world mean more to a man and a woman than to keep the commandment of the Lord in this respect, then they are shutting themselves off from the eternal blessing of increase. … If the responsibilities of parenthood are willfully avoided here, then how can the Lord bestow upon the guilty the blessings of eternal increase? It cannot be, and they shall be denied such blessings.
quotes.note: Printed under the side-head “The Curse of Prevention.” The structure of the argument is what earns the entry: mortal fertility is made the qualifying test for eternal increase, so the two are treated as the same power exercised in two states — the premise that makes the doctrine operative in a talk about contraception rather than a talk about deification. Increase itself is never described; no offspring, no mechanism, no worlds, hence FORWARD-EUPHEMISM. The elision covers three sentences on small families and covenant-breaking; nothing about increase is omitted.

quotes.excerpt: May I make this personal remark: I am the father of eleven children, and to this day every one is a faithful member of the Church and all are active, for that is the way they were taught, and they were obedient. They will belong to me forever and are the foundation stones of my kingdom. My posterity reaches today over the one-hundred mark.
quotes.note: Printed under the side-head “The Blessing of Increase,” which is what fixes the reading: a man's sealed mortal posterity is described as “the foundation stones of my kingdom,” the kingdom being the eternal dominion of an exalted being. That is increase in its domesticated form — no future begetting is claimed, only that this posterity continues and constitutes the kingdom — so FORWARD-EUPHEMISM. Worth pairing with jfs-agq-temple-marriage-1954, where the same man defines eternal lives as “eternal increase—the continuation … of the seeds forever.”

quotes.excerpt: In no other way, other than through birth into this life and the resurrection, can spirits become like our Eternal Father.
quotes.note: Untagged context, and the sentence the rest of the address hangs on: becoming like the Father is gated on embodiment, which is why denying a spirit its body is treated as an offence against the plan rather than a private choice. Theosis only — no claim about how the Father came to be what he is, and none about offspring — so no category, on the same reading that leaves romney-1964-q1 untagged.

notes: Re-pulled verbatim from the Pulpit vault file talks/english/conference-reports/1965/1965-10-smith-my-dear-brethren-and-sisters-i-hope.md, whose body was collated against the DjVu column-order reconstruction of the Church History Library preservation scan (conferencereport1965sa, leaves n27–n30, printed pp. 27–30) in the final-review pass, which repaired a two-column interleaving defect in the opening lines and restored seven printed side-heads. The tagged passages are well clear of the repaired opening. Conference Report, so A. Distinct from the several Answers to Gospel Questions entries by the same author: this is the doctrine delivered as pulpit instruction on birth control to the whole Church, five years before he became President of the Church, and the argument only works because eternal increase is assumed to be continuous with mortal parenthood. The address quotes Brigham Young and Joseph F. Smith on preparing tabernacles for waiting spirits; neither passage has a dataset entry, so no citesId.

title: Sterling W. Sill: God, angels, spirits and men “all of the same species”
speaker: Sterling W. Sill
office: First Council of the Seventy
